bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =陳紀八=

translations.literal: Chen Records 8
translations.idiomatic: Chen Records 8

sentences.zh: 上章困敦，一年。

translations.literal: From Shangzhang Kundun; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: Spanning the year Shangzhang Kundun—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，癸巳，周天元祠太廟。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Zhou Emperor Tianyuan sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on guisi, Northern Zhou's Emperor Tianyuan offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 2戊戌，以左衛將軍任忠為南豫州刺史，督緣江軍防事。

translations.literal: 2. On wuxu, the Left Guard General Ren Zhong was appointed Governor of Southern Yuzhou and put in charge of riverine frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: 2. On wuxu, Left Guard General Ren Zhong was made Governor of Southern Yuzhou with overall command of Yangtze frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 3乙卯，周稅入市者人一錢。

translations.literal: 3. On yimao, Zhou levied a tax of one cash coin on each person entering the market.
translations.idiomatic: 3. On yimao, Zhou imposed a one-cash levy on everyone entering the markets.

sentences.zh: 4二月，丁巳，周天元幸露門學，釋奠。

translations.literal: 4. In the second month, on dingsi, the Zhou Emperor Tianyuan visited the Lumengate Academy and performed the libation sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the second month, on dingsi, Emperor Tianyuan visited the Lumengate Academy for the ceremonial libation to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 5戊午，突厥入貢於周，且迎千金公主。

translations.literal: 5. On wuwu, the Turks presented tribute to Zhou and also came to escort Princess Qianjin.
translations.idiomatic: 5. On wuwu, the Turks brought tribute to Zhou and came to receive Princess Qianjin for marriage.

sentences.zh: 6乙丑，周天元改制為天制，敕為天敕。

translations.literal: 6. On yichou, the Zhou Emperor Tianyuan changed the term zhi (regulations) to tianzhi (Heavenly Regulations) and chi (edicts) to tianchi (Heavenly Edicts).
translations.idiomatic: 6. On yichou, Emperor Tianyuan renamed imperial regulations "Heavenly Regulations" and edicts "Heavenly Edicts."

sentences.zh: 壬午，尊天元皇太后為天元上皇太后，天皇太后為天元聖皇太后。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Tianyuan Empress Dowager was honored as Supreme Tianyuan Empress Dowager, and the Tianhuang Empress Dowager as Sagely Tianyuan Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Tianyuan Empress Dowager was elevated to Supreme Tianyuan Empress Dowager, and the Tianhuang Empress Dowager to Sagely Tianyuan Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔楊后與三后皆稱太皇后，司馬后直稱皇后。

translations.literal: On guiwei, an edict ordered that Empress Yang and the three empresses all be styled Grand Empress, while Empress Sima alone be styled Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, an edict declared that Empress Yang and the three other empresses would all bear the title Grand Empress, while Empress Sima alone would be called simply Empress.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管杞公亮，天元之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: The campaigning commander-in-chief Duke Qi of Qi, Liang, was a cousin once removed of Emperor Tianyuan on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning commander-in-chief Duke Qi of Qi, Yuwen Liang, was Emperor Tianyuan's first cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 其子西陽公溫妻尉遲氏，蜀公迥之孫，有美色，以宗婦入朝。

translations.literal: His son, Duke Xiyang Wen, had as wife Lady Yuchi, granddaughter of Duke Shu Yuwen Jiong; she was beautiful and entered court as a clansman's wife.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Duke Xiyang Wen, had married Lady Yuchi, granddaughter of Duke Shu Yuwen Jiong—a woman of striking beauty who came to court in her capacity as a royal clansman's wife.

sentences.zh: 天元飲之酒，逼而淫之。

translations.literal: Emperor Tianyuan made her drink wine, then forced and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianyuan plied her with wine, then forced himself upon her.

sentences.zh: 亮聞之，懼；

translations.literal: When Liang heard of this, he was afraid;
translations.idiomatic: When Liang learned of this, he was terrified;

sentences.zh: 三月，軍還，至豫州，密謀襲韋孝寬，並其眾，推諸父為主，鼓行而西。

translations.literal: in the third month, as the army returned and reached Yuzhou, he secretly plotted to attack Wei Xiaokuan, absorb his forces, set up one of the imperial uncles as ruler, and march west beating the drums.
translations.idiomatic: in the third month, as his army returned to Yuzhou, he secretly plotted to strike Wei Xiaokuan, absorb his troops, install one of the imperial uncles as emperor, and march west at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 亮國官茹寬知其謀，先告孝寬，孝寬潛設備。

translations.literal: Liang's state retainer Ru Kuan learned of the plot, informed Xiaokuan first, and Xiaokuan secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's staff officer Ru Kuan discovered the plot and warned Xiaokuan in advance; Xiaokuan quietly made his preparations.

sentences.zh: 亮夜將數百騎襲孝寬營，不克而走。

translations.literal: At night Liang led several hundred horsemen in a surprise attack on Xiaokuan's camp but failed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Liang led several hundred cavalry in a night assault on Xiaokuan's camp; when it failed, he fled.

sentences.zh: 戊子，孝寬追斬之，溫亦坐誅。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Xiaokuan pursued and beheaded him; Wen was also executed on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Xiaokuan ran him down and executed him; Wen was put to death as well for his connection to the plot.

sentences.zh: 天元即召其妻入宮，拜長貴妃。

translations.literal: Emperor Tianyuan immediately summoned his wife into the palace and appointed her Senior Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianyuan at once summoned the woman into the palace and made her Senior Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，立亮弟永昌公椿為杞公。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Liang's younger brother Duke Yongchang Chun was established as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Liang's younger brother, Duke Yongchang Chun, was installed as the new Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 周天元如同州，增候正、前驅、式道候為三百六十重。

translations.literal: The Zhou Emperor Tianyuan went to Tongzhou and increased the ranks of outriders, vanguard runners, and ceremonial escorts to three hundred sixty tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianyuan traveled to Tongzhou and expanded the ranks of outriders, vanguard runners, and ceremonial escorts to three hundred and sixty tiers.

sentences.zh: 自應門至於赤岸澤，數十里間，幡旗相蔽，音樂俱作。

translations.literal: From the Ying Gate to Chian Marsh, for several tens of li, banners and flags shut out the sky and music played everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ying Gate to Chian Marsh, for dozens of li, banners blotted out the sky and music sounded without cease.

sentences.zh: 又令虎賁持鈒馬上，稱警蹕。

translations.literal: He also ordered Tiger Guards to hold gongs on horseback and call out the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Tiger Guards ride with clanging gongs, crying the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 乙未，改同州宮為成天宮。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Tongzhou palace was renamed the Palace of Accomplished Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Tongzhou palace was renamed the Palace of Accomplished Heaven.

sentences.zh: 庚子，還長安。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 詔天台侍衛之官，皆著五色及紅、紫、綠衣，以雜色為緣，名曰「品色衣」，有大事，與公服間服之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all Tian Terrace guard officials wear five-colored garments together with red, purple, and green, with mixed colors as trim, called "graded-color robes," to be worn alternately with formal court dress on important occasions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required Tian Terrace guards to wear robes in five colors plus red, purple, and green, trimmed in contrasting hues—these "graded-color robes" were to be worn on ceremonial occasions alongside regular court dress.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔內外命婦皆執笏，其拜宗廟及天台，皆俯伏如男子。

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict ordered that all titled women inside and outside the palace carry tablets; when bowing at the Ancestral Temple and Tian Terrace, they were all to prostrate themselves like men.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, an edict commanded that all titled ladies, within the palace and without, carry ceremonial tablets; when worshipping at the Ancestral Temple and Tian Terrace, they were to prostrate themselves exactly as men did.

sentences.zh: 天元將立五皇后，以問小宗伯狄道辛彥之。

translations.literal: Emperor Tianyuan was about to establish five empresses and asked the Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Xinyan Zhi of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianyuan planned to install five empresses and consulted Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Xinyan Zhi of Didao.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「皇后與天子敵體，不宜有五。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The empress stands as the equal of the Son of Heaven; there should not be five."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The empress is the Son of Heaven's equal in rank; there ought not to be five of them."

sentences.zh: 太學博士西城何妥曰：「昔帝嚳四妃，虞舜二妃。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy erudite He Tuo of Xicheng said, "In antiquity Emperor Ku had four consorts and Emperor Shun had two.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy erudite He Tuo of Xicheng objected: "In antiquity Emperor Ku had four consorts and Emperor Shun had two.

sentences.zh: 先代之數，何常之有！」

translations.literal: The numbers of former ages—how have they ever been fixed!"
translations.idiomatic: How fixed were the numbers of former ages, after all!"

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，免彥之官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and dismissed Xinyan Zhi from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and stripped Xinyan Zhi of his post.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔曰：「坤儀比德，土數惟五，四太皇后外，可增置天中太皇后一人。」

translations.literal: On jiachen, an edict said, "Earthly virtue matches the feminine principle; the number of earth is five alone. Beyond the four Grand Empress Dowagers, one Central Heaven Grand Empress Dowager may be added."
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, an edict declared, "Earthly virtue mirrors the feminine principle, and earth's number is five. Beyond the four Grand Empress Dowagers, one Central Heaven Grand Empress Dowager may now be appointed."

sentences.zh: 於是以陳氏為天中太皇后，尉遲妃為天左太皇后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lady Chen was made Central Heaven Grand Empress Dowager, and Consort Yuchi was made Left Heaven Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was accordingly made Central Heaven Grand Empress Dowager, and Consort Yuchi Left Heaven Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 又造下帳五，使五皇后各居其一，實宗廟祭器於前，自讀祝版而祭之。

translations.literal: He also had five lower tents made so that each of the five empresses dwelt in one; ancestral temple ritual vessels were placed before them, and each read the prayer tablet and performed sacrifice herself.
translations.idiomatic: He also erected five lower tents, one for each empress; ancestral temple vessels were set before them, and each empress read the prayer tablet and conducted her own sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又以五輅載婦人，自帥左右步從。

translations.literal: He also had five imperial carriages carry the women, and he himself led his attendants on foot in their train.
translations.idiomatic: He also had five imperial carriages carry the women, while he himself led his attendants on foot behind them.

sentences.zh: 又好倒懸雞及碎瓦於車上，觀其號呼以為樂。

translations.literal: He also delighted in hanging chickens upside down and breaking tiles on the carriages, watching them cry out for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also amused himself by hanging chickens upside down and smashing tiles from his carriage, delighting in their cries of distress.

sentences.zh: 7夏，四月，癸亥，尚書左僕射陸繕卒。

translations.literal: 7. In summer, the fourth month, on guihai, the Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Lu Chan died.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In summer, the fourth month, on guihai, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Lu Chan died.

sentences.zh: 8己巳，周天元祠太廟；

translations.literal: 8. On jisi, the Zhou Emperor Tianyuan sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: 8. On jisi, Emperor Tianyuan sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 己卯，大雩；

translations.literal: on jimao, a great rain prayer was held;
translations.idiomatic: on jimao, a great rain-prayer ceremony was held;

sentences.zh: 壬午，幸仲山祈雨；

translations.literal: on renwu, he visited Zhong Mountain to pray for rain;
translations.idiomatic: on renwu, he went to Zhong Mountain to pray for rain;

sentences.zh: 甲申，還宮，令京城士女於衢巷作樂迎候。

translations.literal: on jiashen, he returned to the palace and ordered the men and women of the capital to make music in the streets and lanes to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen, he returned to the palace and commanded the men and women of the capital to line the streets with music to welcome him home.

sentences.zh: 9五月，癸巳，以尚書右僕射晉安王伯恭為僕射。

translations.literal: 9. In the fifth month, on guisi, the Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince Jin'an Bo Gong, was appointed Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: 9. In the fifth month, on guisi, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Prince Jin'an Bo Gong was confirmed as Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 10周楊后性柔婉，不妨忌，四皇后及嬪、御等，咸愛而仰之。

translations.literal: 10. The Zhou Empress Yang was gentle and yielding by nature and free of jealousy; the four empresses and all consorts and attendants alike loved and revered her.
translations.idiomatic: 10. Zhou's Empress Yang was gentle and unjealous by nature; the four empresses and all palace ladies alike loved and looked up to her.

sentences.zh: 天元昏暴滋甚，喜怒乖度，嘗譴后，欲加之罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Tianyuan grew ever more muddled and violent; his joy and anger lost all measure, and he once rebuked the empress and wished to punish her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianyuan grew ever more erratic and brutal; his moods swung wildly out of control, and on one occasion he rebuked the empress and meant to punish her.

sentences.zh: 后進止詳閒，辭色不撓，天元大怒，遂賜后死，逼令引訣，后母獨孤氏詣閣陳謝，叩頭流血，然後得免。

translations.literal: The empress's deportment was measured and composed, her words and bearing unyielding; Tianyuan flew into a rage, then bestowed death upon the empress and forced her to take leave. The empress's mother, Lady Dugu, went to the gate to plead forgiveness, knocking her head until it bled, and only then was the empress spared.
translations.idiomatic: The empress remained composed in bearing and unflinching in speech; Tianyuan was enraged and sentenced her to death, forcing her to bid farewell. Her mother, Lady Dugu, came to the palace gate to plead, knocking her head until blood flowed—and only then was the empress spared.

sentences.zh: 后父大前疑堅，位望隆重，天元忌之，嘗因忿謂后曰：「必族滅爾家！」

translations.literal: The empress's father, the Grand Mentor Yang Jian, held eminent rank and prestige; Tianyuan resented him and once said in anger to the empress, "I shall exterminate your whole clan!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father, Grand Mentor Yang Jian, held great rank and prestige; Tianyuan resented him and once said in fury to the empress, "I will wipe out your entire clan!"

sentences.zh: 因召堅，謂左右曰：「色動，即殺之。」

translations.literal: He then summoned Jian and told his attendants, "If his expression changes, kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Jian and told his attendants, "If his face changes color, kill him on the spot."

sentences.zh: 堅至，神色自若，乃止。

translations.literal: When Jian arrived, his bearing was calm and composed, and the emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian arrived, his expression was perfectly calm, and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 內史上大夫鄭譯，與堅少同學，奇堅相表，傾心相結。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat Grand Master Zheng Yi had studied with Jian in youth; he marveled at Jian's bearing and gave him his wholehearted friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Grand Master Zheng Yi had been Jian's schoolmate in youth; struck by Jian's bearing, he gave him his wholehearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 堅既為帝所忌，情不自安，嘗在永巷，私於譯曰：「久願出籓，公所悉也，願少留意！」

translations.literal: Jian, now under the emperor's suspicion, could not feel at ease; once in the Eternal Lane he spoke privately to Yi, saying, "I have long wished to go out to a frontier post—you know this well; I hope you will give it some thought!"
translations.idiomatic: Now under the emperor's suspicion, Jian could not rest easy; once in the Eternal Lane he confided to Yi, "I have long wished to take a provincial post—you know this; please give it some thought!"

sentences.zh: 譯曰：「以公德望，天下歸心。

translations.literal: Yi said, "By your virtue and standing, the hearts of the realm turn to you.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Given your virtue and standing, the hearts of the realm already turn to you.

sentences.zh: 欲求多福，豈敢忘也！

translations.literal: To seek greater fortune—how could I dare forget!
translations.idiomatic: To seek your good fortune—how could I ever forget!

sentences.zh: 謹即言之。」

translations.literal: I shall speak of it at once."
translations.idiomatic: I shall bring it up immediately."

sentences.zh: 天元將遣譯入寇，譯請元帥。

translations.literal: Emperor Tianyuan was about to send Yi on an invasion; Yi requested a commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tianyuan was about to send Yi on campaign against Chen, Yi asked who would command the army.

sentences.zh: 天元曰：「卿意如何？」

translations.literal: Tianyuan said, "What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianyuan asked, "What do you recommend?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若定江東，自非懿戚重臣，無以鎮撫。

translations.literal: He replied, "If we are to secure the lands east of the Yangtze, none but a close kinsman of weight and standing can hold and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To hold the lands east of the Yangtze, nothing less than a senior imperial kinsman can keep order there.

sentences.zh: 可令隨公行，且為壽陽總管以督軍事。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Sui may be sent on the campaign and also made Commander-in-Chief of Shouyang to oversee military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Send the Duke of Sui with the army, and make him Commander-in-Chief of Shouyang to oversee operations."

sentences.zh: 天元從之。

translations.literal: Tianyuan followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以堅為揚州總管，使譯發兵會壽陽。

translations.literal: On jichou, Jian was made Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and Yi was ordered to mobilize troops and join him at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Jian was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and Yi was ordered to mobilize troops and rendezvous with him at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 將行，會堅暴有足疾，不果行。

translations.literal: Just as he was to depart, Jian suddenly fell ill with a foot ailment and did not go after all.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to depart, Jian was suddenly stricken with a severe foot ailment and never went.

sentences.zh: 甲午夜，天元備法駕，幸天興宮。

translations.literal: At midnight on jiawu, Tianyuan arrayed the full imperial equipage and visited the Tianxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on jiawu, Tianyuan rode out in full imperial procession to the Tianxing Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙未，不豫而還。

translations.literal: On yiwei, he fell ill and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, he fell gravely ill and returned.

sentences.zh: 小御正博陵劉昉，素以狡諂得幸於天元，與御正中大夫顏之儀並見親信。

translations.literal: The Junior Imperial Rectifier Liu Fang of Boling had long won Tianyuan's favor through craft and flattery; he and the Imperial Rectifier Grand Master Yan Zhiyi were both trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Imperial Rectifier Liu Fang of Boling had long won Tianyuan's favor through cunning flattery; he and Imperial Rectifier Grand Master Yan Zhiyi were both trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 天元召昉、之儀入臥內，欲屬以後事，天元瘖，不復能言。

translations.literal: Tianyuan summoned Fang and Zhiyi into his sleeping chamber, intending to entrust them with affairs after his death, but Tianyuan was mute and could no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyuan summoned Fang and Zhiyi to his bedside to entrust them with the succession, but he had lost his voice and could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 昉見靜帝幼沖，以楊堅后父，有重名，遂與領內史鄭譯、御飾大夫柳裘、內史大夫杜陵韋謨、御正下士朝那皇甫績謀引堅輔政。

translations.literal: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was young and that Yang Jian, as the empress's father, bore great renown; he then joined with Chief Palace Secretary Zheng Yi, Ornaments Grand Master Liu Qiu, Palace Secretary Grand Master Wei Mo of Duling, and Junior Imperial Rectifier Huangfu Ji of Chaona in a plot to bring in Jian as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was a child and that Yang Jian, the empress's father, commanded great prestige; he joined Chief Palace Secretary Zheng Yi, Ornaments Grand Master Liu Qiu, Palace Secretary Grand Master Wei Mo of Duling, and Junior Imperial Rectifier Huangfu Ji of Chaona in a plot to install Jian as regent.

sentences.zh: 堅固辭，不敢當。

translations.literal: Jian firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jian firmly declined, saying he dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「公若為，速為之；

translations.literal: Fang said, "Sir, if you will act, act quickly;
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "Sir, if you mean to act, act now;

sentences.zh: 不為，昉自為也。」

translations.literal: if not, Fang will act himself."
translations.idiomatic: if not, Fang will act in your place."

sentences.zh: 堅乃從之，稱受詔居中侍疾。

translations.literal: Jian then consented, claiming to have received an edict to attend the emperor at the center and nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then agreed, claiming he had received an edict to remain at the emperor's bedside and tend his illness.

sentences.zh: 裘，惔之孫也。

translations.literal: Qiu was a grandson of Liu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was a grandson of Liu Tan.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝殂。

translations.literal: That day the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪。

translations.literal: The death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: The death was kept secret; no mourning was announced.

sentences.zh: 昉、譯矯詔以堅總知中外兵馬事。

translations.literal: Fang and Yi forged an edict placing Jian in overall charge of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Yi forged an edict placing Jian in overall command of all armies, civil and military.

sentences.zh: 顏之儀知非帝旨，拒而不從。

translations.literal: Yan Zhiyi knew this was not the emperor's intent and refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiyi knew this was not the emperor's true wish and refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 昉等草詔署訖，逼之儀連署，之儀厲聲曰：「主上升遐，嗣子沖幼，阿衡之任，宜在宗英。

translations.literal: Fang and the others drafted the edict and finished signing it, then pressed Zhiyi to sign as well; Zhiyi said in a stern voice, "Our lord has ascended on high; the heir is young and tender. The burden of regency should fall on a worthy of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his allies drafted the edict and signed it, then pressed Zhiyi to add his name; Zhiyi declared in a ringing voice, "Our lord has departed; the heir is a child. The regency belongs to a worthy of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 方今趙王最長，以親以德，合膺重寄。

translations.literal: At present the Prince of Zhao is eldest; in kinship and virtue he should bear this heavy trust.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao is eldest among the princes; in kinship and virtue he is the one who should bear this burden.

sentences.zh: 公等備受朝恩，當思盡忠報國，奈何一旦欲以神器假人！

translations.literal: You gentlemen have all received the court's grace; you should think of giving loyal service to the state—how can you in a single day wish to lend the imperial regalia to another!
translations.idiomatic: You have all received the court's favor; you should be thinking of loyal service to the state—how can you in a single day hand the imperial regalia to an outsider!

sentences.zh: 之儀有死而已，不能誣罔先帝。」

translations.literal: Zhiyi has death and nothing more; he cannot deceive and wrong the late emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi accepts only death; he will not deceive the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 昉等知不可屈。

translations.literal: Fang and the others knew he could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his allies saw he could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 乃代之儀署而行之。

translations.literal: They then signed in Zhiyi's place and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: They signed in his place and issued the edict.

sentences.zh: 諸衛既受敕，並受堅節度。

translations.literal: All the guards, having received the edict, likewise came under Jian's command.
translations.idiomatic: All palace guards, having received the edict, fell under Jian's command.

sentences.zh: 堅恐諸王在外生變，以千金公主將適突厥為辭，征趙、陳、越、代、滕五王入朝。

translations.literal: Jian feared the princes outside the capital might stir up trouble; citing Princess Qianjin's impending marriage to the Turks, he summoned the five princes of Zhao, Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng to court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the princes stationed outside the capital might raise trouble, Jian cited Princess Qianjin's impending marriage to the Turks as pretext to summon the five princes of Zhao, Chen, Yue, Dai, and Teng to court.

sentences.zh: 堅索符璽，顏之儀正色曰：「此天子之物，自有主者，宰相何故索之！」

translations.literal: Jian demanded the imperial seals; Yan Zhiyi said with a stern face, "These are the Son of Heaven's objects; they have their own master—why should the chief minister demand them!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian demanded the imperial seals; Yan Zhiyi said sternly, "These belong to the Son of Heaven and have their rightful keeper—why should a chief minister demand them!"

sentences.zh: 堅大怒，命引出，將殺之；

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angered and ordered him led out to be killed;
translations.idiomatic: Jian was furious and ordered him dragged out for execution;

sentences.zh: 以其民望，出為西邊郡守。

translations.literal: because of his standing among the people, he was instead sent out as governor of a western border commandery.
translations.idiomatic: but because of his popular esteem, he was instead sent out as governor of a western border commandery.

sentences.zh: 丁未，發喪。

translations.literal: On dingwei, mourning was announced.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the emperor's death was formally announced.

sentences.zh: 靜帝入居天台。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing entered and took up residence at the Tian Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing moved into the Tian Terrace.

sentences.zh: 罷正陽宮。

translations.literal: The Zhengyang Palace was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Construction at the Zhengyang Palace was halted.

sentences.zh: 大赦，停洛陽宮作。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared, and work on the Luoyang palace was halted.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared and work on the Luoyang palace was suspended.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，尊阿史那太后為太皇太后，李太后為太帝太后，楊后為皇太后，朱后為帝太后，其陳后、元后、尉遲后並為尼。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Empress Dowager Ashina was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager Li as Grand Imperial Empress Dowager, Empress Yang as Empress Dowager, and Empress Zhu as Imperial Empress Dowager; Empresses Chen, Yuan, and Yuchi were all made nuns.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Empress Dowager Ashina was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager Li to Grand Imperial Empress Dowager, Empress Yang to Empress Dowager, and Empress Zhu to Imperial Empress Dowager; Empresses Chen, Yuan, and Yuchi were all forced to take Buddhist vows.

sentences.zh: 以漢王贊為上柱國、右大丞相，尊以虛名，實無所綜理。

translations.literal: Prince Han Zan was made Senior Pillar of State and Right Grand Chancellor, honored in name only with no actual administration.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han Zan was named Senior Pillar of State and Right Grand Chancellor—a title of honor with no real authority.

sentences.zh: 以楊堅為假黃鉞、左大丞相，秦王贄為上柱國。

translations.literal: Yang Jian was made Acting Holder of the Golden Axe and Left Grand Chancellor; Prince Qin Zan was made Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was made Acting Holder of the Golden Battle-Axe and Left Grand Chancellor; Prince Qin Zan was named Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 百官總己以聽於左丞相。

translations.literal: All officials gathered their affairs and took orders from the Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: All officials turned their affairs over to the Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 堅初受顧命，使邗國公楊惠謂御正下大夫李德林曰：「朝廷賜令總文武事，經國任重。

translations.literal: When Jian first received the dying emperor's charge, he sent Duke Hanguo Yang Hui to tell the Junior Imperial Rectifier Li Delin, "The court has granted you overall charge of civil and military affairs; governing the state is a weighty burden.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian first received the regency, he sent Duke Hanguo Yang Hui to tell Junior Imperial Rectifier Li Delin, "The court has placed you in charge of all civil and military affairs; governing the state is a grave responsibility.

sentences.zh: 今欲與公共事，必不得辭。」

translations.literal: I now wish to share the work with you; you must not decline."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to share this burden with you; you must not refuse."

sentences.zh: 德林曰：「願以死奉公。」

translations.literal: Delin said, "I am willing to serve you unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Delin replied, "I will serve you unto death."

sentences.zh: 堅大喜。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 始，劉昉、鄭譯議以堅為大塚宰，譯自攝大司馬，昉又求小塚宰。

translations.literal: At the outset, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had planned to make Jian Grand Chamberlain, with Yi himself taking the post of Grand Marshal, while Fang sought the post of Junior Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi had planned to make Jian Grand Chamberlain, with Yi taking the Grand Marshal's post for himself and Fang seeking the Junior Chamberlain's office.

sentences.zh: 堅私問德林曰：「欲何以見處？」

translations.literal: Jian privately asked Delin, "How do you think I should be treated?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian took Li Delin aside and asked, "How do you think I ought to be positioned?"

sentences.zh: 德林曰：「宜作大丞相、假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事，不爾，無以壓眾心。」

translations.literal: Delin said, "You should be made Grand Chancellor, granted acting use of the yellow battle-axe, and appointed Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without; otherwise there is no way to suppress the hearts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin replied, "You should be made Grand Chancellor, given the yellow battle-axe in acting capacity, and named supreme commander of all forces at court and in the provinces. Without that, you will never hold the people's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 及發喪，即依此行之。

translations.literal: When the mourning was announced, he immediately acted according to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the death was formally announced, he did exactly that.

sentences.zh: 以正陽宮為丞相府。

translations.literal: He made Zhenyang Palace the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He established his chancellery in Zhenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 時眾情未壹，堅引司武上士盧賁置左右。

translations.literal: At that time popular sentiment was not yet unified; Jian had Supervising Martial Senior Attendant Lu Ben brought to his side.
translations.idiomatic: Popular opinion was still divided, so Yang Jian kept Supervising Martial Senior Attendant Lu Ben at his side.

sentences.zh: 將之東宮，百官皆不知所從。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to the Eastern Palace, all the officials did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out for the Eastern Palace, the officials had no idea which side to take.

sentences.zh: 堅潛令賁部伍仗衛，因召公卿，謂曰：「欲求富貴者宜相隨。」

translations.literal: Jian secretly ordered Ben to array troops with weapons as guards, then summoned the high ministers and said, "Those who wish for wealth and rank should follow along."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian quietly had Lu Ben muster armed guards, then summoned the chief ministers and told them, "Whoever wants wealth and rank should come with me."

sentences.zh: 往往偶語，欲有去就。

translations.literal: Here and there they whispered among themselves, wanting to leave or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Men murmured in small groups, uncertain whether to go or stay.

sentences.zh: 賁嚴兵而至，眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: Ben arrived with stern troops, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben marched up with a disciplined force, and no one dared move.

sentences.zh: 出崇陽門，至東宮，門者拒不納，賁諭之，不去；

translations.literal: They went out through Chongyang Gate and reached the Eastern Palace; the gatekeepers refused to admit them, and though Ben admonished them, they would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: They passed through Chongyang Gate and reached the Eastern Palace, where the gatekeepers refused them entry; Lu Ben ordered them aside, but they would not budge.

sentences.zh: 嗔目叱之，門者遂卻，堅入。

translations.literal: He glared and shouted at them, and the gatekeepers then fell back; Jian entered.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed them with a glare and shouted them down, and the gatekeepers finally stepped aside; Yang Jian went in.

sentences.zh: 賁遂典丞相府宿衛。

translations.literal: Ben then took charge of night guards at the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben was then put in charge of the chancellery's night watch.

sentences.zh: 賁，辯之弟子也。

translations.literal: Ben was a disciple of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ben had been a disciple of Lu Bian.

sentences.zh: 以鄭譯為丞相府長史，劉昉為司馬，李德林為府屬，二人由是怨德林。

translations.literal: He appointed Zheng Yi as chief administrator of the chancellor's office, Liu Fang as marshal, and Li Delin as a staff officer; the two men therefore resented Delin.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zheng Yi chief administrator of the chancellery, Liu Fang marshal, and Li Delin a staff officer; Zheng and Liu took a dislike to Delin from that moment on.

sentences.zh: 內史下大夫勃海高熲明敏有器局，習兵事，多計略，堅欲引之入府，遣楊惠諭意。

translations.literal: Inner Scribe Lower Grandee Gao Jiong of Bohai was perceptive and quick-witted, with breadth of vision; skilled in military affairs and possessing many stratagems, Jian wished to bring him into the office and sent Yang Hui to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong of Bohai, an Inner Scribe Lower Grandee, was sharp-minded and far-seeing, well versed in war and rich in stratagems. Yang Jian wanted him in the chancellery and sent Yang Hui to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 熲承旨，欣然曰：「願受驅馳。

translations.literal: Jiong received the instruction and said with pleasure, "I am willing to be driven and run at your command.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong accepted the message and said gladly, "I am yours to command.

sentences.zh: 縱令公事不成，熲亦不辭滅族。」

translations.literal: Even if the public affair does not succeed, Jiong will not shrink from extermination of his clan."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the enterprise fails, I will not flinch from the destruction of my whole house."

sentences.zh: 乃以為相府司錄。

translations.literal: He was then made chief clerk of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed chief clerk of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時漢王贊居禁中，每與靜帝同帳而坐。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Han Zan resided inside the forbidden palace and each day sat under the same canopy with Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Zan was then living inside the palace and sat under the same canopy with Emperor Jing every day.

sentences.zh: 劉昉飾美妓進贊，贊甚悅之。

translations.literal: Liu Fang adorned beautiful courtesans and presented them to Zan; Zan was greatly pleased with them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang dressed up beautiful entertainers and sent them to Zan, who was delighted with them.

sentences.zh: 昉因說贊曰：「大王，先帝之弟，時望所歸。

translations.literal: Fang then urged Zan, saying, "Your Highness is the late emperor's younger brother, to whom the hopes of the age turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then pressed his case: "Your Highness is the late emperor's own brother—the man the age looks to.

sentences.zh: 孺子幼沖，豈堪大事！

translations.literal: The young child is tender in years—how can he bear great affairs!
translations.idiomatic: That child on the throne is too young to bear the weight of rule!

sentences.zh: 今先帝初崩，人情尚擾。

translations.literal: Now that the late emperor has just died, popular sentiment is still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor has only just died, and the realm is still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 王且歸第，待事寧後，入為天子，此萬全計也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness should for now return to your residence; after affairs are settled, enter and become Son of Heaven—this is a plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw to your own residence for now. Once things calm down, you can enter and take the throne. That is the surest course."

sentences.zh: 贊年少，性識庸下，以為信然，遂從之。

translations.literal: Zan was young, and his nature and understanding were mediocre; he believed it to be true and therefore followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was young and not very bright; he took this for good counsel and did as Fang said.

sentences.zh: 堅革宣帝苛酷之政，更為寬大，刪略舊律，作《刑書要制》，奏而行之；

translations.literal: Jian abolished Emperor Xuan's harsh and cruel policies and replaced them with leniency; he abridged the old laws and drew up Essentials of Penal Law, memorialized it, and put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian swept away Emperor Xuan's harsh rule and replaced it with a milder one. He trimmed the old statutes and drafted Essentials of Penal Law, which he submitted and put into force.

sentences.zh: 躬履節儉，中外悅之。

translations.literal: He personally practiced thrift, and both court and countryside were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly himself, and people throughout the court and the realm approved.

sentences.zh: 堅夜召太史中大夫庾季才，問曰：「吾以庸虛，受茲顧命。

translations.literal: Jian summoned at night Director of the Imperial Astronomy Bureau Yu Jicai and asked, "I, mediocre and unworthy, have received this dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yang Jian summoned Yu Jicai, Director of the Imperial Astronomy Bureau, and asked, "I am a mediocre man who has been handed this deathbed trust.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，卿以為何如？」

translations.literal: Heaven's timing and human affairs—what do you think of them?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you make of Heaven's signs and the state of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「天道精微，難可意察。

translations.literal: Jicai said, "The way of Heaven is subtle and profound, hard to discern by intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai replied, "Heaven's way is too subtle to read by guesswork alone.

sentences.zh: 竊以人事卜之，符兆已定。

translations.literal: I venture to prognosticate by human affairs—the omens are already fixed.
translations.idiomatic: But if I judge by what men are doing, the signs are already set.

sentences.zh: 季才縱言不可，公豈復得為箕、穎之事乎！」

translations.literal: Even if Jicai were to say it is impossible, could you still do what was done at Ji and Ying!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I were to say otherwise, could you still wash your ears in the Ying and retire to Mount Ji like Xu You?"

sentences.zh: 堅默然久之，曰：「誠如君言。」

translations.literal: Jian was silent for a long time, then said, "Truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was silent a long while, then said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 獨孤夫人亦謂堅曰：「大事已然，騎虎之勢，必不得下，勉之！」

translations.literal: Lady Dugu also said to Jian, "The great affair has already happened; in the posture of riding a tiger, you cannot dismount—press on!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dugu told him as well, "The die is cast. Once you are riding a tiger, there is no getting off. Press forward!"

sentences.zh: 堅以相州總管尉遲迥位望素重，恐有異圖，使迥子魏安公惇奉詔書召之會葬。

translations.literal: Jian, because Xiang Province Area Commander Yuwen Jiong's position and prestige had long been great, feared he might have other designs; he had Jiong's son, Duke of Wei'an Dun, bring an imperial edict summoning him to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong, area commander of Xiang Province, was a man of long-standing rank and prestige, and Yang Jian feared he might have designs of his own. He had Jiong's son, Duke of Wei'an Dun, deliver an imperial summons to bring him to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以上柱國韋孝寬為相州總管；

translations.literal: On renzi, he appointed Upper Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan as area commander of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he named Upper Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan area commander of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 又以小司徒叱列長義為相州刺史，先令赴鄴；

translations.literal: He also made Junior Minister of Education Chilie Changyi governor of Xiang Province and ordered him to go first to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Junior Minister of Education Chilie Changyi governor of Xiang Province and sent him ahead to Ye.

sentences.zh: 孝寬續進。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan continued to advance afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan followed after.

sentences.zh: 陳王純時鎮齊州，堅使門正上士崔彭征之。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chun was then stationed at Qi Province; Jian sent Gate Inspector Senior Attendant Cui Peng to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chen Chun was then holding Qi Province, and Yang Jian sent Gate Inspector Senior Attendant Cui Peng to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 彭以兩騎往止傳捨，遣人召純。

translations.literal: Peng went with two horsemen and stopped at a relay station, then sent a man to summon Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Peng rode in with two escorts, halted at a relay station, and sent for Chun.

sentences.zh: 純至，彭請屏左右，密有所道，遂執而鎖之，因大言曰：「陳王有罪，詔征入朝，左右不得輒動！」

translations.literal: When Chun arrived, Peng asked that attendants be dismissed and privately conveyed something; he then seized and shackled him, and shouted, "Prince of Chen is guilty; by edict he is summoned to court—attendants must not stir!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chun arrived, Cui Peng dismissed the attendants as if to speak in confidence, then seized and shackled him. He shouted, "Prince of Chen stands accused. By imperial order he is summoned to court. No one move!"

sentences.zh: 其從者愕然而去。

translations.literal: His followers, stunned, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His followers stood stunned, then fell back.

sentences.zh: 彭，楷之孫也。

translations.literal: Peng was a grandson of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Peng was a grandson of Cui Kai.

sentences.zh: 六月，五王皆至長安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, all five princes reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month all five princes arrived in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 11庚申，周復行佛、道二教。

translations.literal: 11. On gengshen, Zhou again permitted the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: 11. On gengshen Zhou restored Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 舊沙門、道士精志者，簡令入道。

translations.literal: Former Buddhist monks and Daoist priests of refined resolve were selected and ordered to enter the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Former monks and priests of proven devotion were screened and allowed to resume their orders.

sentences.zh: 12周尉遲迥知丞相堅將不利於帝室，謀舉兵討之。

translations.literal: 12. Yuwen Jiong of Zhou learned that Chancellor Jian would be harmful to the imperial house and plotted to raise troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: 12. Yuwen Jiong saw that Chancellor Yang Jian meant to harm the imperial house and began plotting to raise an army against him.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬至朝歌，迥遣其大都督賀蘭貴，繼書候韋孝寬。

translations.literal: When Wei Xiaokuan reached Chaoge, Jiong sent his Grand Area Commander Helan Gui and letters in succession to inquire after Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiaokuan reached Chaoge, Jiong sent his grand area commander Helan Gui with repeated messages to greet him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬留貴與語以審之，疑其有變，遂稱疾徐行；

translations.literal: Xiaokuan detained Gui and spoke with him to investigate; suspecting there was trouble, he then claimed illness and traveled slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan kept Helan Gui with him and questioned him closely. Smelling trouble, he pleaded illness and slowed his march.

sentences.zh: 又使人至相州求醫藥，密以伺之。

translations.literal: He also sent men to Xiang Province to seek medicine, secretly to spy on the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to Xiang Province on the pretext of fetching medicine, using them to watch what was happening.

sentences.zh: 孝寬兄子藝，為魏郡守，迥遣藝迎孝寬，孝寬問迥所為，藝黨於迥，不以實對。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's elder brother's son Yi was prefect of Wei Commandery; Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan. Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was doing; Yi sided with Jiong and did not answer truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan's nephew Yi was prefect of Wei Commandery. Jiong sent Yi to meet him, but when Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was up to, Yi, who sided with Jiong, lied.

sentences.zh: 孝寬怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was angry and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan flew into a rage and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 藝懼，悉以迥謀語孝寬。

translations.literal: Yi, in fear, told Xiaokuan all of Jiong's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yi told Wei Xiaokuan everything about Jiong's plot.

sentences.zh: 孝寬攜藝西走，每至亭驛，盡驅傳馬而去，謂驛司曰：「蜀公將至，宜速具酒食。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan took Yi and fled westward; at every relay station he drove off all relay horses and left, telling the station officials, "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive—you should quickly prepare food and drink."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan fled west with Yi in tow. At every relay station he seized all the post horses and rode on, telling the clerks, "The Duke of Shu is coming. Have food and wine ready at once."

sentences.zh: 迥尋遣儀司大將軍梁子康將數百騎追孝寬，追者至驛，輒逢盛饌，又無馬，遂遲留不進。

translations.literal: Jiong soon sent Grand General of the Ceremonial Office Liang Zikang with several hundred horsemen in pursuit of Xiaokuan; when the pursuers reached each station they always found lavish feasts, and with no horses they therefore lingered and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong soon sent Grand General of the Ceremonial Office Liang Zikang after him with several hundred horsemen. At every station the pursuers found a lavish spread waiting and no horses to ride, so they fell further and further behind.

sentences.zh: 孝寬與藝由是得免。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan and Yi thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Wei Xiaokuan and Yi got away.

sentences.zh: 堅又令候正破六韓裒詣迥諭旨，密與總管府長史晉昶等書，令為之備。

translations.literal: Jian also ordered Houzheng Polu Hanpi to go to Jiong and convey the imperial intent, and secretly wrote to Chief Administrator of the Area Command Jin Chang and others, ordering them to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian also sent Houzheng Polu Hanpi to Jiong with an official message, while secretly writing to Jin Chang, chief administrator of the area command, and others to ready themselves.

sentences.zh: 迥聞之，殺昶及裒；

translations.literal: When Jiong learned of this, he killed Chang and Hanpi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong learned of this, he executed Jin Chang and Hanpi.

sentences.zh: 集文武士民，登城北樓，令之曰：「楊堅藉後父之勢，挾幼主以作威福，不臣之跡，暴於行路。

translations.literal: He assembled civil and military officials and the people, ascended the north tower of the city wall, and addressed them, saying, "Yang Jian, relying on the power of being the empress's father, holds the young ruler to wield authority and blessings for himself; his disloyal conduct is exposed on the public road.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered officials, soldiers, and townspeople, mounted the north gate tower, and proclaimed, "Yang Jian has used his position as the empress's father to seize power through a child emperor. His treason is plain for all on the road to see.

sentences.zh: 吾與國舅甥，任兼將相；

translations.literal: I am nephew to the empress's brother and hold offices of both general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: I am the empress's nephew by marriage, entrusted with both civil and military command.

sentences.zh: 先帝處吾於此，本欲寄以安危。

translations.literal: The late emperor placed me here precisely intending to entrust me with the realm's safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor posted me here to safeguard the realm in its hour of danger.

sentences.zh: 今欲與卿等糾合義勇，以匡國庇民，何如？」

translations.literal: Now I wish to join with you in gathering righteous volunteers to set the state right and shelter the people—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to rally loyal men among you to restore the state and protect the people. Will you follow me?"

sentences.zh: 眾鹹從命。

translations.literal: All obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd assented as one.

sentences.zh: 迥乃自稱大總管，承製置官司。

translations.literal: Jiong then styled himself Grand Area Commander and, acting on imperial orders, established government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong declared himself Grand Area Commander and, claiming imperial authority, set up a full government apparatus.

sentences.zh: 時趙王招入朝，留少子在國，迥奉以號令。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Zhao had entered court and left his youngest son in the province; Jiong upheld him to issue orders.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Zhao was then at court and had left his youngest son in the province; Jiong used the boy to lend his regime legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 甲子，堅發關中兵，以韋孝寬為行軍元帥，郕公梁士彥、樂安公元諧、化政公宇文忻、濮陽公武川宇文述、武鄉公崔弘度、清河公楊素、隴西公李詢等皆為行軍總管，以討迥。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Jian mobilized the troops of Guanzhong, making Wei Xiaokuan campaign commander-in-chief; Duke of Ye Liang Shiyan, Duke of Le'an Yuan Xie, Duke of Huazheng Yuwen Xin, Duke of Puyang Wuchuan Yuwen Shu, Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu, Duke of Qinghe Yang Su, Duke of Longxi Li Xun, and others were all made campaign area commanders to attack Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Yang Jian mobilized the armies of Guanzhong. He made Wei Xiaokuan supreme field commander and named Duke of Ye Liang Shiyan, Duke of Le'an Yuan Xie, Duke of Huazheng Yuwen Xin, Duke of Puyang Wuchuan Yuwen Shu, Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu, Duke of Qinghe Yang Su, Duke of Longxi Li Xun, and others as campaign commanders to crush Jiong.

sentences.zh: 弘度，楷之孫；

translations.literal: Hongdu was a grandson of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongdu was a grandson of Cui Kai.

sentences.zh: 詢，穆之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xun was a nephew of Mu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was a nephew of Li Mu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝使計部中大夫楊尚希撫慰山東，至相州，聞宣帝殂，與尉遲迥發喪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xuan had sent Director of the Accounting Bureau Yang Shangxi to console and reassure the region east of the mountains; when he reached Xiang Province and heard that Emperor Xuan had died, he joined Yuwen Jiong in announcing the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xuan had sent Yang Shangxi, Director of the Accounting Bureau, to reassure the eastern provinces. When he reached Xiang Province and learned the emperor was dead, he joined Yuwen Jiong in proclaiming the mourning.

sentences.zh: 尚希出，謂左右曰：「蜀公哭不哀而視不安，將有他計。

translations.literal: When Shangxi went out, he said to those beside him, "The Duke of Shu weeps without grief and his gaze is restless—he must have another plan.
translations.idiomatic: On his way out Shangxi told his attendants, "The Duke of Shu mourns without sorrow and keeps shifting his eyes. He is planning something else.

sentences.zh: 吾不去，懼及於難。」

translations.literal: If I do not leave, I fear I will be caught in disaster."
translations.idiomatic: If I stay, I am afraid I will be caught up in it."

sentences.zh: 遂夜從捷徑而遁。

translations.literal: He then fled by night along a shortcut.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slipped away by a back road.

sentences.zh: 遲明，迥覺，追之不及，遂歸長安。

translations.literal: By dawn Jiong noticed; he pursued but could not overtake him, and Shangxi returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Jiong realized what had happened and gave chase, but could not catch him. Shangxi made it back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅遣尚希督宗兵三千人鎮潼關。

translations.literal: Jian sent Shangxi to command three thousand clan troops to garrison Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sent Shangxi with three thousand clan troops to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 雍州牧畢剌王賢，與五王謀殺堅，事洩，堅殺賢，並其三子，掩五王之謀不問。

translations.literal: Yong Province Governor Prince of Bila Xian, together with the five princes, plotted to kill Jian; when the affair leaked out, Jian killed Xian together with his three sons and covered up the five princes' plot without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bila Xian, governor of Yong Province, joined the five princes in a plot to kill Yang Jian. When it was exposed, Yang Jian executed Xian and his three sons, then hushed up the other princes' involvement.

sentences.zh: 以秦王贄為大塚宰，杞公椿為大司徒。

translations.literal: He made Prince of Qin Zan Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi Chun Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince of Qin Zan Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi Chun Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以柱國梁睿為益州總管。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he made Pillar of State Liang Rui area commander of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he named Pillar of State Liang Rui area commander of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 睿，御之子也。

translations.literal: Rui was a son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rui was a son of Liang Yu.

sentences.zh: 13周遣汝南公神慶、司衛上士長孫晟送千金公主於突厥。

translations.literal: 13. Zhou sent Duke of Runan Shen Qing and Supervising Guard Senior Attendant Zhangsun Sheng to escort Princess Qianjin to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: 13. Zhou dispatched Duke of Runan Shen Qing and Supervising Guard Senior Attendant Zhangsun Sheng to escort Princess Qianjin to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 晟，幼之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sheng was a great-grandson of You.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng was a great-grandson of Zhangsun You.

sentences.zh: 又遣建威侯賀若誼賂佗缽可汗，且說之以求高紹義。

translations.literal: Zhou also sent Marquis of Jianwei He Ruo Yi to bribe Khan Tuoban and moreover persuade him to hand over Gao Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also sent Marquis of Jianwei He Ruo Yi to bribe Khan Tuoban and persuade him to surrender Gao Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 佗缽偽與紹義獵於南境，使誼執之。

translations.literal: Tuoban pretended to hunt with Shaoyi on the southern frontier and had Yi seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoban feigned a hunting expedition with Shaoyi on the southern border and had He Ruo Yi take him captive.

sentences.zh: 誼，敦之弟子也。

translations.literal: Yi was a disciple of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Yi had been a disciple of He Dun.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲申，紹義至長安，徙之蜀；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen, Shaoyi reached Chang'an and was relocated to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiashen, Gao Shaoyi arrived in Chang'an and was exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 久之，病死於蜀。

translations.literal: After a long time he died of illness in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died of illness in Shu.

sentences.zh: 14周青州總管尉遲勤，迥之弟也。

translations.literal: 14. Yuwen Qin, area commander of Qing Province in Zhou, was Jiong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: 14. Yuwen Qin, Zhou's area commander of Qing Province, was Yuwen Jiong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 初得迥書，表送之，尋亦從迥。

translations.literal: When he first received Jiong's letter, he memorialized and forwarded it; soon afterward he also followed Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When he first received Jiong's letter he forwarded it to court in a memorial, but soon joined the rebellion himself.

sentences.zh: 迥所統相、衛、黎、洺、貝、趙、冀、瀛、滄、勤所統青、齊、膠、光、莒等州皆從之，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: The provinces under Jiong's command—Xiang, Wei, Li, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and those under Qin's command—Qing, Qi, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all followed him; their forces numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces under Jiong's command—Xiang, Wei, Li, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and those under Qin—Qing, Qi, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all rose with him. Their combined forces ran into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史邵公冑，申州刺史李惠，東楚州刺史費也利進，潼州刺史曹孝遠，各據本州，徐州總管司錄席毘羅據兗州，前東平郡守畢義緒據蘭陵，皆應迥；

translations.literal: Governor of Xing Province Duke of Shao Zhou, Governor of Shen Province Li Hui, Governor of Eastern Chu Province Fei Yeli Jin, Governor of Tong Province Cao Xiaoyuan each held his own province; Chief Clerk of the Xu Province Area Command Xi Piluo held Yan Province; former Administrator of Dongping Commandery Bi Yixu held Lanling—all responded to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Xing Province Duke of Shao Zhou, Governor of Shen Province Li Hui, Governor of Eastern Chu Province Fei Yeli Jin, and Governor of Tong Province Cao Xiaoyuan each seized his province. Xi Piluo, chief clerk of the Xu Province area command, took Yan Province; Bi Yixu, former administrator of Dongping Commandery, held Lanling. All of them rallied to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 懷縣永橋鎮將紇豆陵惠以城降迥。

translations.literal: Hedouling Hui, garrison commander of Yongqiao in Huai County, surrendered the city to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Hedouling Hui, commander of Yongqiao garrison in Huai County, surrendered his post to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 迥使其所署大將軍石遜攻建州，建州刺史宇文弁以州降之。

translations.literal: Jiong sent his appointed Grand General Shi Xun to attack Jian Province; Governor of Jian Province Yuwen Bian surrendered the province to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent his appointee Grand General Shi Xun against Jian Province, and Governor Yuwen Bian surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 又遣西道行台韓長業攻拔潞州，執刺史趙威，署城人郭子勝為刺史。

translations.literal: He also sent Western Route Commissioner Han Changye to capture Lu Province, seized Governor Zhao Wei, and appointed a man of the city, Guo Zisheng, as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Western Route Commissioner Han Changye to take Lu Province, captured Governor Zhao Wei, and installed a local man, Guo Zisheng, as governor.

sentences.zh: 紇豆陵惠襲陷鉅鹿，遂圍恆州。

translations.literal: Hedouling Hui raided and captured Julu, then besieged Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hedouling Hui stormed Julu and then laid siege to Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 上大將軍宇文威攻汴州，莒州刺史烏丸尼等帥青、齊之眾圍沂州，大將軍檀讓攻拔曹、亳二州，屯兵梁郡。

translations.literal: Senior Grand General Yuwen Wei attacked Bian Province; Governor of Ju Province Wuhwan Ni and others led the forces of Qing and Qi in besieging Yi Province; Grand General Tan Rang captured Cao and Bo provinces and encamped at Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Grand General Yuwen Wei attacked Bian Province. Governor of Ju Province Wuhwan Ni led Qing and Qi troops against Yi Province. Grand General Tan Rang seized Cao and Bo provinces and encamped at Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 席毘羅眾號八萬，軍於蕃城，攻陷昌慮、下邑。

translations.literal: Xi Piluo's forces were said to number eighty thousand; he encamped at Fancheng and captured Changyu and Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Piluo's army was said to number eighty thousand men. He camped at Fancheng and took Changyu and Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 李惠自申州攻永州，拔之。

translations.literal: Li Hui from Shen Province attacked Yong Province and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: From Shen Province Li Hui attacked Yong Province and took it.

sentences.zh: 迥遣使招大左輔、并州刺史李穆，穆鎖其使，封上其書。

translations.literal: Jiong sent envoys to recruit Grand Left Assistant and Governor of Bing Province Li Mu; Mu shackled his envoys and sealed and forwarded their letter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent envoys to win over Grand Left Assistant Li Mu, governor of Bing Province. Mu put the envoys in chains and forwarded their letter sealed to court.

sentences.zh: 穆子士榮，以穆所居天下精兵處，陰勸穆從迥，穆深拒之。

translations.literal: Mu's son Shirong, because the place where Mu resided was where the realm's elite troops were stationed, secretly urged Mu to follow Jiong; Mu firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's son Shirong, knowing that Bing Province held the empire's best troops, secretly urged his father to join Jiong. Li Mu refused outright.

sentences.zh: 堅使內史大夫柳裘詣穆，為陳利害，又使穆子左侍上士渾往布腹心。

translations.literal: Jian sent Inner Scribe Grandee Liu Qiu to Mu to set forth advantages and harms, and also sent Mu's son, Left Attendant Senior Attendant Hun, to lay bare his inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sent Inner Scribe Grandee Liu Qiu to Li Mu to explain the stakes, and also sent Mu's son, Left Attendant Senior Attendant Hun, to speak for him in the frankest terms.

sentences.zh: 穆使渾奉尉斗於堅，曰：「願執威柄以尉安天下。」

translations.literal: Mu had Hun present the commander's baton to Jian, saying: "I wish you would take hold of authority to comfort and pacify the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu had Hun present the commander's baton to Yang Jian, saying, "I wish you would take up authority and bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 又十三環金帶遺堅。

translations.literal: He also sent Jian the thirteen-ring gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yang Jian the thirteen-ring gold belt.

sentences.zh: 十三環金帶者，天子之服也。

translations.literal: The thirteen-ring gold belt was the regalia of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen-ring gold belt was an emblem reserved for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，遣渾詣韋孝寬述穆意。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased and sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan to convey Mu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was greatly pleased and sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan to convey Li Mu's intent.

sentences.zh: 穆兄子崇，為懷州刺史，初欲應迥；

translations.literal: Mu's elder brother's son Chong, who was governor of Huaizhou, at first wished to join Jiong;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu's nephew Chong, governor of Huaizhou, at first wished to join Yuwen Jiong;

sentences.zh: 後知穆附堅，慨然太息曰：「闔家富貴者數十人，值國有難，竟不能扶傾繼絕，復何面目處天地間乎！」

translations.literal: Later, learning that Mu had sided with Jian, he sighed deeply and said: "Several tens in our household enjoy wealth and rank; facing national crisis, we cannot even shore up the tottering and carry on the extinct line—what face have we left to dwell between heaven and earth!"
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Li Mu had sided with Yang Jian, he sighed deeply and said, "Several dozen of us in this house enjoy wealth and rank, yet in a time of national crisis we cannot even shore up what is falling or carry on what is broken—what face have we left to show under heaven and earth!

sentences.zh: 不得已亦附於堅。

translations.literal: Having no choice, he too submitted to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: With no other choice, he too submitted to Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 迥子誼，為朔州刺史，穆執送長安；

translations.literal: Jiong's son Yi, who was governor of Shuozhou—Mu apprehended him and sent him to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong's son Yi, governor of Shuozhou, Li Mu seized and sent to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 又遣兵討郭子勝，擒之。

translations.literal: He also dispatched troops against Guo Zisheng and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent troops against Guo Zisheng and captured him.

sentences.zh: 迥招徐州總管源雄、東郡守於仲文，皆不從。

translations.literal: Jiong recruited Xu Province governor Yuan Xiong and Dong Commandery magistrate Yu Zhongwen, but neither obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong tried to win over Xu Province governor Yuan Xiong and Dong Commandery magistrate Yu Zhongwen, but neither would follow him.

sentences.zh: 雄，賀之曾孫；

translations.literal: Xiong was the great-grandson of He;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was the great-grandson of He;

sentences.zh: 仲文，謹之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhongwen was the grandson of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was the grandson of Jin.

sentences.zh: 迥遣宇文冑自石濟，宇文威自白馬濟河，二道攻仲文，仲文棄郡走還長安，迥殺其妻子。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Yuwen Zhou to cross at Shiji and Yuwen Wei to cross at Baima; the two columns attacked Zhongwen. Zhongwen abandoned the commandery and fled back to Chang'an, and Jiong killed his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong sent Yuwen Zhou to cross at Shiji and Yuwen Wei to cross at Baima; the two columns attacked Zhongwen. Zhongwen abandoned his post and fled to Chang'an, and Jiong killed his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 迥遣檀讓徇地河南，丞相堅以仲文為河南道行軍總管，使詣洛陽發兵討讓，命楊素討宇文冑。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Tan Rang to overrun Henan. Chancellor Jian appointed Zhongwen Grand Marshal for the Henan Route, sent him to Luoyang to raise troops against Rang, and ordered Yang Su to attack Yuwen Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong sent Tan Rang to sweep through Henan. Chancellor Yang Jian made Zhongwen Grand Marshal for the Henan Route, sent him to Luoyang to raise troops against Rang, and ordered Yang Su to attack Yuwen Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，周以丞相堅都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Zhou made Chancellor Jian commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Northern Zhou made Chancellor Yang Jian commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 鄖州總管司馬消難亦舉兵應迥，己酉，周以柱國王誼為行軍元帥，以討消難。

translations.literal: Yunzhou governor Sima Xiaonan also raised troops in support of Jiong. On jiyou, Zhou appointed Pillar of State Wang Yi campaign marshal to attack Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhou governor Sima Xiaonan also raised troops in support of Yuwen Jiong. On jiyou, Zhou appointed Pillar of State Wang Yi campaign marshal to attack Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史于顗，仲文之兄也，與總管趙文表不協；

translations.literal: Guangzhou governor Yu Yi, Zhongwen's elder brother, was on bad terms with governor Zhao Wenbiao;
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou governor Yu Yi, Zhongwen's elder brother, was at odds with governor Zhao Wenbiao;

sentences.zh: 詐得心疾，誘文表，手殺之，因唱言文表與尉遲迥通謀。

translations.literal: He feigned heart disease to lure Wenbiao, killed him with his own hand, and then proclaimed that Wenbiao had conspired with Yuwen Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned heart disease to lure Wenbiao in, killed him with his own hand, and then proclaimed that Wenbiao had been in league with Yuwen Jiong.

sentences.zh: 堅以迥未平，因勞勉之，即拜吳州總管。

translations.literal: Since Jiong was not yet suppressed, Jian rewarded and encouraged him and immediately appointed him governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuwen Jiong had not yet been suppressed, Yang Jian praised and encouraged him and immediately appointed him governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙僭王招謀殺堅，邀堅過其第，堅繼酒淆就之。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Zhao Zhao plotted to kill Jian and invited Jian to visit his residence. Jian, already tipsy from wine, went along.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Zhao Zhao plotted to kill Yang Jian and invited him to his residence. Yang Jian, already drunk, went along.

sentences.zh: 招引入寢室，招子員、貫及妃弟魯封等皆在左右，佩刀而立，又藏刃於帷席之間，伏壯士於室後。

translations.literal: Zhao brought him into the bedchamber. Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan and his consort's younger brother Lu Feng and others stood at his sides with swords drawn. Blades were hidden among curtains and bedding, and stalwart men lay in wait behind the room.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao led him into the bedchamber. Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan, his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, and others stood at hand with swords drawn. Blades were hidden among curtains and bedding, and strongmen lay in wait behind the room.

sentences.zh: 堅左右皆不得從，唯從祖弟開府儀同大將軍弘、大將軍元冑坐於戶側。

translations.literal: None of Jian's attendants were permitted to follow. Only his younger cousin from the clan line, Opening Grand General of Equal Rank Hong, and Grand General Yuan Zhou sat by the door.
translations.idiomatic: None of Yang Jian's attendants was allowed to follow. Only his cousin, Opening Grand General of Equal Rank Hong, and Grand General Yuan Zhou sat by the door.

sentences.zh: 冑，順之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhou was the grandson of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was the grandson of Shun.

sentences.zh: 弘、冑皆有勇力，為堅腹心。

translations.literal: Hong and Zhou were both brave and strong, trusted intimates of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Zhou were both brave and strong, trusted confidants of Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，招以佩刀刺瓜連啖堅，欲因而刺之。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Zhao sliced melon with his girdle sword and repeatedly offered pieces to Jian, intending to strike him in the course of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, Zhao sliced melon with his girdle sword and kept offering pieces to Yang Jian, intending to stab him in the act.

sentences.zh: 元冑進曰：「相府有事，不可久留。」

translations.literal: Yuan Zhou stepped forward and said: "There is business at the chancellery; we cannot stay long."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhou stepped forward and said, "There is urgent business at the chancellery—we cannot stay long."

sentences.zh: 招訶之曰：「我與丞相言，汝何為者！」

translations.literal: Zhao berated him: "I am speaking with the Chancellor—what are you doing here!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao scolded him: "I am speaking with the Chancellor—what are you doing here!"

sentences.zh: 叱之使卻。

translations.literal: He shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted at him to step back.

sentences.zh: 冑嗔目憤氣，扣刀入衛。

translations.literal: Zhou glared in fury, hand on his sword, and entered to guard Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou glared in fury, hand on his sword, and entered to guard Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 招賜之酒，曰：「吾豈有不善之意邪！」

translations.literal: Zhao offered him wine, saying: "Surely I have no ill intent!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao offered him wine, saying, "Surely I mean you no harm!

sentences.zh: 卿何猜警如是？」

translations.literal: Why are you so suspicious and on guard?
translations.idiomatic: Why are you so suspicious and on guard?

sentences.zh: 招偽吐，將入後邠，冑恐其為變，扶令上坐，如此再三。

translations.literal: Zhao feigned vomiting and made to go to the rear courtyard. Zhou, fearing treachery, supported him back to his seat—this happened again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao pretended to vomit and made to go to the rear courtyard. Zhou, fearing treachery, supported him back to his seat—this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 招偽稱喉乾，命冑就廚取飲，冑不動。

translations.literal: Zhao falsely claimed his throat was dry and ordered Zhou to fetch drink from the kitchen. Zhou did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao claimed his throat was dry and ordered Zhou to fetch drink from the kitchen. Zhou did not budge.

sentences.zh: 會滕王逌後至，堅降價迎之。

translations.literal: Just then Prince of Teng You arrived later. Jian humbly went out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Prince of Teng You arrived. Yang Jian went out in person to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 冑耳語曰：「事勢大異，可速去！」

translations.literal: Zhou whispered: "The situation is greatly changed—leave at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou whispered, "The situation has changed completely—leave at once!"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「彼無兵馬，何能為！」

translations.literal: Jian said: "He has no armed force—what can he do!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian said, "He has no troops—what can he do!"

sentences.zh: 冑曰：「兵馬皆彼物，彼若先發，大事去矣！

translations.literal: Zhou said: "The armed men are all his. If he strikes first, the whole affair is lost!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "The armed men are all his men. If he strikes first, everything is lost!

sentences.zh: 冑不辭死，恐死無益。」

translations.literal: Zhou did not shrink from death, but feared dying without benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou did not shrink from death, but feared dying to no purpose."

sentences.zh: 堅復入坐。

translations.literal: Jian sat down again.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sat down again.

sentences.zh: 冑聞室後有被甲聲，遽請曰：「相府事殷，公何得如此！」

translations.literal: Zhou heard the clink of armor from behind the room and urgently said: "The chancellery is pressed with business—how can you linger so!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou heard the clink of armor from behind the room and urgently said, "The chancellery is pressed with business—how can you linger like this!"

sentences.zh: 因扶堅下床趨去。

translations.literal: He thereupon helped Jian down from the couch and hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon helped Yang Jian down from the couch and hurried away.

sentences.zh: 招將追之。

translations.literal: Zhao was about to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was about to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 冑以身蔽戶，招不得出；

translations.literal: Zhou blocked the door with his body; Zhao could not get out;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou blocked the door with his body, and Zhao could not get out;

sentences.zh: 堅及門，冑自後至。

translations.literal: Jian reached the door; Zhou came up from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian reached the door; Zhou came up from behind.

sentences.zh: 招恨不時發，彈指出血。

translations.literal: Zhao regretted that he had not acted in time and snapped his finger until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao regretted that he had not acted in time and snapped his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 壬子，堅誣招與越野王盛謀反，皆殺之，及其諸子。

translations.literal: On renzi, Jian falsely charged Zhao and Prince of Yue Sheng with plotting rebellion. All were executed, along with their sons.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Yang Jian falsely charged Zhao and Prince of Yue Sheng with plotting rebellion. All were executed, along with their sons.

sentences.zh: 賞賜元冑，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhou was rewarded with gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhou was rewarded with gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 周室諸王數欲伺隙殺堅，堅都督臨涇李圓通常保護之，由是得免。

translations.literal: The princes of the Zhou house repeatedly sought openings to kill Jian. Jian's commander of Linjing Li Yuantong constantly protected him, and thus he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of the Zhou house repeatedly looked for chances to kill Yang Jian. His commander of Linjing, Li Yuantong, constantly protected him, and so he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，周主封其弟衍為葉王，術為郢王。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Zhou ruler enfeoffed his younger brothers Yan as Prince of Ye and Shu as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Zhou ruler enfeoffed his younger brothers Yan as Prince of Ye and Shu as Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 周豫、荊、襄三州蠻反，攻破郡縣。

translations.literal: In Zhou, the tribesmen of Yu, Jing, and Xiang three provinces rebelled and stormed commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou, the tribal peoples of Yu, Jing, and Xiang provinces rebelled and overran commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 周韋孝寬軍至永橋城，諸將請先攻之。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan's Zhou army reached Yongqiao city. The generals asked to attack it first.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan's army reached Yongqiao. The generals asked to attack it first.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「城小而固，若攻而不拔，損我兵威。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "The city is small but solid. If we attack and fail to take it, our martial prestige will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan said, "The city is small but strong. If we attack and fail to take it, our martial prestige will suffer.

sentences.zh: 今破其大軍，此何能為！」

translations.literal: If we now smash their main army, what can this place do!"
translations.idiomatic: If we smash their main army now, what can this place do!"

sentences.zh: 於是引軍壁於武陟。

translations.literal: He therefore led his army to fortify at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore led his army to encamp at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥遣其子魏安公惇帥眾十萬入武德，軍於沁東。

translations.literal: Yuwen Jiong sent his son Duke of Wei'an Dun leading one hundred thousand men into Wude, encamping east of the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong sent his son, Duke of Wei'an Dun, at the head of one hundred thousand men into Wude, and encamped east of the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 會沁水漲，孝寬與迥隔水相持不進。

translations.literal: As the Qin River swelled, Xiaokuan and Jiong faced each other across the water without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin River rose, Xiaokuan and Yuwen Jiong faced each other across the water without advancing.

sentences.zh: 孝寬長史李詢密啟丞相堅云：「梁士彥、宇文忻、崔弘度並受尉遲迥餉金，軍中慅慅，人情大異。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's chief administrator Li Xun secretly reported to Chancellor Jian: "Liang Shiyan, Yuwen Xin, and Cui Hongdu all accepted bribes of gold from Yuwen Jiong. The army is restless and morale is greatly unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's chief administrator Li Xun secretly reported to Chancellor Yang Jian: "Liang Shiyan, Yuwen Xin, and Cui Hongdu all accepted gold from Yuwen Jiong. The army is restless and morale is greatly shaken."

sentences.zh: 堅深以為憂，與內史上大夫鄭譯謀代此三人者，李德林曰：「公與諸將，皆國家貴臣，未相服從，今正以挾令之威控御之耳。

translations.literal: Jian was deeply worried and consulted Inner Scribe Grandee Zheng Yi about replacing the three. Li Delin said: "You and these generals are all eminent ministers of the state and do not yet defer to one another. You now control them only by the authority of holding the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was deeply worried and consulted Inner Scribe Grandee Zheng Yi about replacing the three. Li Delin said, "You and these generals are all eminent ministers of the state and do not yet defer to one another. You control them now only by the authority of the edict you hold.

sentences.zh: 前所遣者，疑其乖異，後所遣者，又安知其能盡腹心邪！

translations.literal: Those sent before you were suspected of disloyalty; those you send afterward—how can you know they will give their whole hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Those you sent before were suspected of disloyalty; those you send afterward—how can you know they will give you their whole hearts?

sentences.zh: 又，取金之事，虛實難用，今一旦代之，或懼罪逃逸；

translations.literal: Besides, the matter of taking gold is hard to verify. If you replace them at once, some may fear punishment and flee;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the charge of taking gold is hard to verify. If you replace them at once, some may fear punishment and flee;

sentences.zh: 若加縻縶，則自鄖公以下，莫不驚疑。

translations.literal: If you add restraint and bondage, from Duke of Yun downward none will fail to be alarmed and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If you add restraint and bondage, from the Duke of Yun downward none will fail to be alarmed and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 且臨敵易將，此燕、趙之所以敗也。

translations.literal: Moreover, changing commanders on the eve of battle—this is why Yan and Zhao were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, changing commanders on the eve of battle—this is why Yan and Zhao were defeated.

sentences.zh: 如愚所見，但遣公一腹心，明於智略，素為諸將所信服者，速至軍所，使觀其情偽。

translations.literal: In my humble view, send only one trusted confidant of yours, skilled in strategy and long respected by the generals, to reach the army quickly and observe their true disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, send only one trusted confidant of yours, skilled in strategy and long respected by the generals, to reach the army quickly and observe their true disposition.

sentences.zh: 縱有異意，必不敢動，動亦能制之矣。」

translations.literal: Even if disloyal intent exists, they will not dare act; if they act, he can still restrain them."
translations.idiomatic: Even if disloyal intent exists, they will not dare act; if they act, he can still restrain them."

sentences.zh: 堅大悟，曰：「公不發此言，幾敗大事。」

translations.literal: Jian saw the point clearly and said: "Had you not spoken these words, I would nearly have ruined the great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian saw the point clearly and said, "Had you not spoken these words, I would nearly have ruined the great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 乃命少內史崔仲方往監諸軍，為之節度。

translations.literal: He then ordered Junior Inner Scribe Cui Zhongfang to go oversee the armies and direct their movements.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Junior Inner Scribe Cui Zhongfang to go oversee the armies and direct their movements.

sentences.zh: 仲方，猷之子也，辭以父在山東。
