translations.literal: Zhongfang was the son of You. He declined on the ground that his father was in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was the son of You. He declined on the ground that his father was in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 又命劉昉、鄭譯昉，辭以未嘗為將，譯辭以母老。

translations.literal: He then ordered Liu Fang and Zheng Yi—Fang declined, saying he had never been a general; Yi declined, citing an aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Liu Fang and Zheng Yi—Fang declined, saying he had never been a general; Yi declined, citing an aged mother.

sentences.zh: 堅不悅。

translations.literal: Jian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was displeased.

sentences.zh: 府司錄高熲請行，堅喜，遣之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the office Gao Jiong volunteered to go. Jian was pleased and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the office Gao Jiong volunteered to go. Yang Jian was pleased and sent him.

sentences.zh: 熲受命亟發，遣人辭母而已。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong received the commission and set out at once, sending someone only to bid farewell to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong received the commission and set out at once, sending someone only to bid farewell to his mother.

sentences.zh: 自是堅措置軍事，皆與李德林謀之，時軍書日以百數，德林口授數人，文意百端，不加治點。

translations.literal: From then on Jian arranged all military affairs in consultation with Li Delin. Military dispatches then numbered in the hundreds daily. Delin dictated to several scribes at once; the wording covered every contingency without need for revision.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yang Jian arranged all military affairs in consultation with Li Delin. Military dispatches then numbered in the hundreds daily. Delin dictated to several scribes at once; the wording covered every contingency without need for revision.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難以鄖、隨、溫、應、土、順、沔、儇、岳九州及魯山等八鎮來降，遺其子為質以求援。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan surrendered with the nine provinces of Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying, Tu, Shun, Mian, Xuan, and Yue and eight garrisons including Lushan, sending his son as hostage to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan surrendered to Chen with the nine provinces of Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying, Tu, Shun, Mian, Xuan, and Yue and eight garrisons including Lushan, sending his son as a hostage to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 八月，己未，詔以消難為大都督、總督九州八鎮諸軍事、司空，賜爵隨公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiwei, an edict appointed Xiaonan Grand Commander, overall commander of the nine provinces and eight garrisons, and Minister of Works, and bestowed the title Duke of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiwei, Chen issued an edict appointing Sima Xiaonan Grand Commander, overall commander of the nine provinces and eight garrisons, and Minister of Works, and bestowed on him the title Duke of Sui.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔鎮西將軍樊毅進督沔、漢諸軍事，南豫州刺史任忠帥眾趣歷陽，超武將軍陳慧紀為前軍都督，趣南兗州。

translations.literal: On gengshen, an edict made Frontier General Fan Yi advance to supervise Mian and Han military affairs; Southern Yuzhou governor Ren Zhong led troops toward Liyang; Chaowu General Chen Huiji served as vanguard commander toward Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Chen issued an edict making Frontier General Fan Yi advance to supervise Mian and Han military affairs; Southern Yuzhou governor Ren Zhong led troops toward Liyang; Chaowu General Chen Huiji served as vanguard commander toward Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周益州總管王謙亦不附丞相堅，起巴、蜀之兵以攻始州。

translations.literal: Wang Qian, Zhou governor of Yizhou, also would not submit to Chancellor Jian. He raised Ba and Shu troops to attack Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian, Zhou governor of Yizhou, also would not submit to Chancellor Yang Jian. He raised Ba and Shu troops to attack Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 梁睿至漢川，不得進，堅即以睿為行軍元帥以討謙。

translations.literal: Liang Rui reached Hanchuan but could not advance. Jian immediately made Rui campaign marshal to attack Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rui reached Hanchuan but could not advance. Yang Jian immediately made Rui campaign marshal to attack Qian.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔以司馬消難為大都督水陸諸軍事。

translations.literal: On wuchen, an edict made Sima Xiaonan Grand Commander of all land and water forces.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Chen issued an edict making Sima Xiaonan Grand Commander of all land and water forces.

sentences.zh: 庚午，通直散騎常侍淳於陵克臨江郡。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Direct-and-Regular Palace Attendant Chunyu Ling captured Linjiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Direct-and-Regular Palace Attendant Chunyu Ling captured Linjiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁世宗使中書舍人柳莊奉書入周。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Liang sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Liu Zhuang bearing a letter into Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Liang sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Liu Zhuang bearing a letter into Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丞相堅執莊手曰：「孤昔以開府，從役江陵，深蒙梁主殊眷。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jian took Zhuang's hand and said: "When I was a mere opening office holder following the campaign at Jiangling, I received the Liang ruler's exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Jian took Zhuang's hand and said, "When I was a mere opening office holder on the Jiangling campaign, I received the Liang ruler's exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 今主幼時艱，猥蒙顧托。

translations.literal: The present ruler is young and faces hard times; I have undeservedly received the charge of regency.
translations.idiomatic: The present ruler is young and faces hard times; I have undeservedly received the charge of regency.

sentences.zh: 梁主奕葉委誠朝廷，當相與共保歲寒。」

translations.literal: The Liang ruler for generation after generation has pledged loyalty to the court. We should together preserve our bond through the cold season.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler for generation after generation has pledged loyalty to the court. We should together preserve our bond through the cold season.

sentences.zh: 時諸將競勸梁主舉兵，與尉遲迥連謀，以為進可以盡節周氏，退可以席捲山南。

translations.literal: Just then generals were all urging the Liang ruler to raise troops and join in conspiracy with Yuwen Jiong, arguing that advancing could fulfill loyalty to the Zhou house, while retreating could sweep up the lands south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Just then generals were all urging the Liang ruler to raise troops and join in conspiracy with Yuwen Jiong, arguing that advancing could fulfill loyalty to the Zhou house, while retreating could sweep up the lands south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 梁主疑未決。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 會莊至，具道堅語，且曰：「昔袁紹、劉表、王凌、諸葛誕，皆一時雄傑，據要地，擁強兵，然功業莫就，禍不旋踵者，良由魏、晉挾天子，保京都，仗大順以為名故也。

translations.literal: When Zhuang arrived, he fully conveyed Jian's words and also said: "In the past Yuan Shao, Liu Biao, Wang Ling, and Zhuge Dan were heroes of their age. They held strategic ground and commanded strong armies, yet their achievements came to nothing and disaster followed swift on their heels—precisely because Wei and Jin held the Son of Heaven, guarded the capital, and wielded the mandate of legitimacy as their banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang arrived, he fully conveyed Yang Jian's words and also said, "In the past Yuan Shao, Liu Biao, Wang Ling, and Zhuge Dan were heroes of their age. They held strategic ground and commanded strong armies, yet their achievements came to nothing and disaster followed swift on their heels—precisely because Wei and Jin held the Son of Heaven, guarded the capital, and wielded the mandate of legitimacy as their banner.

sentences.zh: 今尉遲迥雖曰舊將，昏耄已甚；

translations.literal: Today Yuwen Jiong, though called an old general, is already deep in senility;
translations.idiomatic: Today Yuwen Jiong, though called an old general, is already deep in senility;

sentences.zh: 司馬消難、王謙，常人之下者，非有匡合之才。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan and Wang Qian are men below the ordinary and lack talent to unite the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan and Wang Qian are men below the ordinary and lack talent to unite the realm.

sentences.zh: 周朝將相，多為身計，競效節於楊氏。

translations.literal: Zhou court ministers and generals mostly look to their own interest and vie to declare loyalty to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou court ministers and generals mostly look to their own interest and vie to declare loyalty to the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 以臣料之，迥等終當覆滅，隨公必移周祚。

translations.literal: By my reckoning, Jiong and the others will in the end be overthrown, and Duke of Sui will surely transfer Zhou's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, Yuwen Jiong and the others will in the end be overthrown, and the Duke of Sui will surely transfer Zhou's mandate.

sentences.zh: 未若保境息民，以觀其變。」

translations.literal: Better to hold your borders, give the people rest, and watch how affairs change.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold your borders, give the people rest, and watch how affairs change.

sentences.zh: 梁主深然之，眾議遂止。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler deeply agreed, and the clamor of counsel ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler deeply agreed, and the clamor of counsel ceased.

sentences.zh: 高熲至軍，為橋於沁水。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong reached the army and built a bridge across the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong reached the army and built a bridge across the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 尉遲惇於上流縱火筏，熲豫為土狗以御之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Dun sent fire-rafts downstream from the upper river. Gao Jiong had prepared earthen water-blocks in advance to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dun sent fire-rafts downstream from the upper river. Gao Jiong had prepared earthen water-blocks in advance to block them.

sentences.zh: 惇布陳二十餘里，麾兵少卻，欲待孝寬軍半渡而擊之；

translations.literal: Dun deployed battle lines over twenty li, ordered his troops to fall back slightly, intending to wait until Xiaokuan's army was half across and then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Dun deployed battle lines over twenty li, ordered his troops to fall back slightly, intending to wait until Wei Xiaokuan's army was half across and then strike.

sentences.zh: 孝寬因其卻，鳴鼓齊進。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, seeing the withdrawal, sounded drums and advanced all together.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan, seeing the withdrawal, sounded drums and advanced all together.

sentences.zh: 軍既渡，熲命焚橋，以絕士卒反顧之心。

translations.literal: Once the army had crossed, Gao Jiong ordered the bridge burned to cut off any thought of turning back among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army had crossed, Gao Jiong ordered the bridge burned to cut off any thought of turning back among the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 惇兵大敗，單騎走。

translations.literal: Dun's army was utterly defeated; he fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's army was utterly defeated; he fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乘勝進，追至鄴。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan pressed the victory in pursuit as far as Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan pressed the victory in pursuit as far as Ye.

sentences.zh: 庚午，迥與惇及惇弟西都公祐，悉將其卒十三萬陳於城南，迥別統萬人，皆綠巾、錦襖，號「黃龍兵」。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Jiong with Dun and Dun's younger brother Duke of Xidu You mustered all their troops, one hundred thirty thousand, and formed battle lines south of the city. Jiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all in green headcloths and brocade jackets, called the "Yellow Dragon Army."
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Yuwen Jiong with Dun and Dun's younger brother, Duke of Xidu You, mustered all their troops, one hundred thirty thousand, and formed battle lines south of the city. Jiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all in green headcloths and brocade jackets, called the "Yellow Dragon Army."

sentences.zh: 迥弟勤帥眾五萬，自青州赴迥，以三千騎先至。

translations.literal: Jiong's younger brother Qin led fifty thousand troops from Qingzhou to join Jiong, with three thousand cavalry arriving first.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong's younger brother Qin led fifty thousand men from Qingzhou to reinforce him, and three thousand horsemen reached the field ahead of the main body.

sentences.zh: 迥素習軍旅，老猶被甲臨陳。

translations.literal: Jiong had long been versed in military affairs; even in old age he still donned armor and went to the battlefront.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong was a lifelong soldier; even in his old age he still put on armor and took his place at the front of the battle line.

sentences.zh: 其麾下兵皆關中人，為之力戰，孝寬等軍不利而卻。

translations.literal: The troops under his command were all men from Guanzhong; they fought fiercely for him, and Xiaokuan's army met with no success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers under his command were all men from Guanzhong, and they fought for him with desperate valor; Wei Xiaokuan's forces fared poorly and fell back.

sentences.zh: 鄴中士民觀戰者數萬人，行軍總管宇文忻曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians in Ye watched the battle. Campaign commander Yuwen Xin said: "The situation is desperate!
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians in Ye had come out to watch the fighting. Campaign commander Yuwen Xin said, "The situation is desperate!

sentences.zh: 吾當以詭道破之。」

translations.literal: I shall use deceit to break them."
translations.idiomatic: I must break them by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 乃先射觀者，觀者皆走，轉相騰藉，聲如雷霆。

translations.literal: He then first shot arrows at the spectators; the spectators all fled, trampling one another in succession, the noise like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his archers to fire into the crowd of onlookers. The spectators all fled, trampling one another in waves, until the uproar rolled like thunder.

sentences.zh: 忻乃傳呼曰：「賊敗矣！」

translations.literal: Xin then had the cry passed along: "The rebels are defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin then had the cry passed down the ranks: "The rebels are routed!"

sentences.zh: 眾復振，因其擾而乘之。

translations.literal: The troops rallied again, and taking advantage of the disturbance, pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: His men took heart again, and he seized on the chaos to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 迥軍大敗，走保鄴城。

translations.literal: Jiong's army was utterly defeated and fled to hold Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong's army was shattered and fled back into Ye to make a stand.

sentences.zh: 孝寬縱兵圍之，李詢及思安伯代人賀婁子幹先登。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan unleashed his troops to besiege it. Li Xun and the Baron of Si'an, Helou Zigan of the Dai people, were the first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan sent his troops to invest the city. Li Xun and Helou Zigan, Baron of Si'an, a man of the Dai, were the first over the walls.

sentences.zh: 崔弘度妹，先適迥子為妻，及鄴城破，迥窘迫升樓，弘度直上龍尾追之。

translations.literal: Cui Hongdu's younger sister had previously been given in marriage to Jiong's son. When Ye fell, Jiong, hard pressed, ascended a tower; Hongdu went straight up the Dragon Tail ramp in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongdu's younger sister had earlier been married to Yuwen Jiong's son. When Ye fell, Jiong, cornered, climbed a tower; Hongdu went straight up the Dragon Tail ramp after him.

sentences.zh: 迥彎弓，將射弘度。

translations.literal: Jiong drew his bow, about to shoot Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong bent his bow and was about to shoot Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 弘度脫兜鍪，謂迥曰：「頗相識不？

translations.literal: Hongdu removed his helmet and said to Jiong: "Do you recognize me at all?
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu took off his helmet and said to Jiong, "Do you know me at all?

sentences.zh: 今日各圖國事，不得顧私。

translations.literal: Today each of us serves the national cause; we cannot indulge private feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Today each of us must answer to the state; private ties cannot be indulged.

sentences.zh: 以親戚之情，謹遏亂兵，不許侵辱。

translations.literal: Out of family ties, I have strictly restrained the disorderly troops and forbidden them to molest or insult anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for our kinship, I have kept the unruly soldiers in check and forbidden them to plunder or abuse anyone.

sentences.zh: 事勢如此，早為身計，何所侍也？」

translations.literal: Matters stand as they do—make early provision for yourself. What are you waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: Things have come to this pass—look to your own end. What are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 迥擲弓於地，罵左丞相極口而自殺。

translations.literal: Jiong threw his bow to the ground, cursed the Left Chancellor with every foul word, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong threw his bow to the ground, cursed Left Chancellor Yang Jian with every foul word he knew, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 弘度顧其弟弘升曰：「汝可取迥頭。」

translations.literal: Hongdu turned to his younger brother Hongsheng and said: "You may take Jiong's head."
translations.idiomatic: Hongdu turned to his younger brother Hongsheng and said, "You take Jiong's head."

sentences.zh: 弘升斬之。

translations.literal: Hongsheng cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng struck it off.

sentences.zh: 軍士在小城中者，孝寬盡坑之。

translations.literal: The soldiers who were in the inner citadel—Xiaokuan had them all buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers who had held the inner citadel—Wei Xiaokuan had every one of them buried alive.

sentences.zh: 勤、惇、祐東走青州，未至，開府儀同大將軍郭衍追獲之。

translations.literal: Qin, Dun, and You fled east toward Qingzhou. Before they arrived, General of the Gate with Equal Honor Guo Yan pursued and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Dun, and You fled east toward Qingzhou, but before they could reach it, General Guo Yan overtook and captured them.

sentences.zh: 丞相堅以勤初有誠款，特不之罪。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jian, because Qin had at first shown sincere good faith, specially did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Jian, because Qin had at the outset shown sincere loyalty, made a special exception and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 李惠先自縛歸罪，堅復其官爵。

translations.literal: Li Hui first bound himself and came to confess guilt; Jian restored his office and title.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui had already bound himself and surrendered to accept punishment; Yang Jian restored his rank and title.

sentences.zh: 迥末年衰耄，及起兵，以小御正崔達拏為長史。

translations.literal: In his final years Jiong had become senile. When he raised troops, he appointed the minor official Cui Danao as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years Yuwen Jiong had grown feeble-minded; when he took up arms, he made the minor official Cui Danao his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 達拏，暹之子也，文士，無籌略，舉措多失，凡六十八日而敗。

translations.literal: Danao was Xian's son, a literary man without strategic ability; his actions were mostly mistaken, and in all of sixty-eight days he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Danao was the son of Xian—a man of letters, without strategic sense, whose decisions were mostly wrong—and the whole rebellion collapsed in sixty-eight days.

sentences.zh: 於仲文軍至蓼隄，去梁郡七里。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen's army reached Liaodi, seven li from Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen's army reached Liaodi, seven li from Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 檀讓擁眾數萬，仲文以羸師挑戰而偽北，讓不設備；

translations.literal: Tan Rang commanded tens of thousands of men. Zhongwen used a weakened force to offer battle and feigned retreat; Rang made no preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang had tens of thousands of men under him. Zhongwen offered battle with a weakened force and then feigned retreat; Rang took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 仲文還擊，大破之，生獲五千餘人，斬首七百級。

translations.literal: Zhongwen turned and struck back, inflicting a great defeat; more than five thousand were captured alive and seven hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen wheeled about and attacked, routing the enemy; more than five thousand were taken alive and seven hundred heads were counted.

sentences.zh: 進攻梁郡，迥守將劉子寬棄城走。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack on Liang commandery; Jiong's defending general Liu Zikuan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Liang commandery, where Jiong's defending general Liu Zikuan abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 仲文進擊曹州，獲迥所署刺史李仲康。

translations.literal: Zhongwen advanced to attack Cao prefecture and captured Li Zhongkang, the governor Jiong had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen advanced against Cao prefecture and captured Li Zhongkang, the governor Yuwen Jiong had installed.

sentences.zh: 檀讓以餘眾屯成武，仲文襲擊，破之，遂拔成武。

translations.literal: Tan Rang encamped the remnant force at Chengwu. Zhongwen made a surprise attack, defeated him, and then took Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang gathered the survivors at Chengwu. Zhongwen fell on them by surprise, broke their force, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 迥將席毘羅，眾十萬屯沛縣，將攻徐州。

translations.literal: Jiong's general Xi Piruo, with a force of one hundred thousand, encamped at Pei county and was about to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong's general Xi Piruo had one hundred thousand men at Pei county and was preparing to strike at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其妻子在金鄉，仲文遣人詐為毘羅使者，謂金鄉城主徐善淨曰：「檀讓明日午時至金鄉，宣蜀公令，賞賜將士。」

translations.literal: His wife and children were at Jinxiang. Zhongwen sent a man disguised as Piruo's messenger to tell Jinxiang's magistrate Xu Shanjing: "Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang at noon tomorrow to announce the Duke of Shu's order and reward the officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were at Jinxiang. Zhongwen sent a man posing as Piruo's envoy to tell Jinxiang's magistrate Xu Shanjing, "Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang at noon tomorrow to proclaim the Duke of Shu's orders and reward the troops."

sentences.zh: 金鄉人皆喜。

translations.literal: The people of Jinxiang were all delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jinxiang were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 仲文簡精兵，偽建迥旗幟，倍道而進。

translations.literal: Zhongwen selected elite troops, raised Jiong's banners in pretense, and marched at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen picked elite troops, flew Yuwen Jiong's banners as a ruse, and marched at forced pace.

sentences.zh: 善淨望見，以為檀讓，出迎謁。

translations.literal: Shanjing saw them from afar, took them for Tan Rang, and went out to greet them.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjing saw them from a distance, took them for Tan Rang's force, and went out to receive them.

sentences.zh: 仲文執之，遂取金鄉。

translations.literal: Zhongwen seized him and then took Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen seized him on the spot and took Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 諸將多勸屠其城，仲文曰：「此城乃毘羅起兵之所，當寬其妻子，其兵自歸。

translations.literal: Many of the generals urged that the city be slaughtered. Zhongwen said: "This city is where Piruo raised his troops; we should treat his wife and children leniently, and his soldiers will surrender of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his officers urged him to slaughter the city. Zhongwen said, "This is the place where Piruo raised his army. If we treat his wife and children with mercy, his soldiers will come over of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 如即屠之，彼望絕矣。」

translations.literal: If we slaughter it at once, their hope will be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: If we massacre them now, they will have nothing left to hope for."

sentences.zh: 眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: All praised the plan as good.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed that this was wise.

sentences.zh: 於是毘羅恃眾來薄官軍，仲文設伏擊之，毘羅眾大潰，爭投洙水死，水為之不流。

translations.literal: Thereupon Piruo, relying on his numbers, came to press the government army. Zhongwen set an ambush and struck him; Piruo's host collapsed in great disorder, men scrambling to throw themselves into the Zhushui and drown until the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: When Piruo, trusting to his numbers, came up to engage the imperial army, Zhongwen laid an ambush and broke him. Piruo's force disintegrated; men threw themselves into the Zhushui in such numbers that the river ceased to run.

sentences.zh: 獲檀讓，檻送京師；

translations.literal: Tan Rang was captured and sent to the capital in a cage;
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang was taken alive and sent to the capital in a cage;

sentences.zh: 斬毘羅，傳首。

translations.literal: Piruo was beheaded and his head sent about.
translations.idiomatic: Piruo was beheaded and his head was sent about as proof.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬分兵討關東叛者，悉平之。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan divided his troops to attack the rebels in the eastern passes and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan sent columns against the rebels east of the passes and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 堅徙相州於安陽，毀鄴城及邑居。

translations.literal: Jian moved Xiang province to Anyang and destroyed Ye city together with its settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian moved Xiang province to Anyang and demolished Ye city and its surrounding towns.

sentences.zh: 分相州，置毛州、魏州。

translations.literal: He divided Xiang province and established Mao and Wei provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He partitioned what had been Xiang province and created Mao and Wei provinces.

sentences.zh: 梁主聞迥敗，謂柳莊曰：「若從眾人之言。

translations.literal: When the Liang ruler heard of Jiong's defeat, he said to Liu Zhuang: "Had we followed the counsel of the multitude,
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang emperor heard that Yuwen Jiong had been defeated, he said to Liu Zhuang, "Had we listened to the crowd,

sentences.zh: 社稷已不守矣！」

translations.literal: the altars of state would already have been lost!"
translations.idiomatic: the altars of state would already have fallen!"

sentences.zh: 丞相堅之初得政也，待黃公劉昉、沛公鄭譯甚厚，賞賜不可勝計，委以心膂，朝野傾屬，稱為「黃、沛」。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Jian first seized power, he treated Duke of Huang Liu Fang and Duke of Pei Zheng Yi with great favor; rewards beyond counting were given, and they were entrusted as his innermost confidants. Court and common people looked to them, and they were called "Huang and Pei."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian first took hold of power, he treated Liu Fang, Duke of Huang, and Zheng Yi, Duke of Pei, with extraordinary generosity—rewards beyond counting—and entrusted them as his closest confidants. All eyes in court and country turned to them, and men spoke of "Huang and Pei."

sentences.zh: 二人皆恃功驕恣，溺於財利，不親職務。

translations.literal: Both relied on their achievements and grew arrogant and unrestrained, drowning in wealth and profit and neglecting their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Both grew arrogant on the strength of their service, wallowed in gain, and neglected their offices.

sentences.zh: 及辭監軍，堅始疏之，恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: When they resigned from overseeing the army, Jian began to keep them at a distance, and favor and courtesy gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: Once they gave up their role as military overseers, Yang Jian began to distance himself from them, and his favor grew noticeably cooler.

sentences.zh: 高熲自軍所還，寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong returned from the army, and day by day his favor and treatment grew more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong returned from the front, his standing at court rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 時王謙、司馬消難未平，堅憂之，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan had not yet been suppressed; Jian worried over this and forgot both sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan were still in rebellion, and Yang Jian brooded over it until he could neither eat nor sleep.

sentences.zh: 而昉逸游縱酒，相府事多遺落。

translations.literal: Yet Fang wandered about in idleness and drank to excess, and many matters at the chancellor's office were neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Fang roamed about in idleness and drank without restraint, and business at the chancellor's office piled up unattended.

sentences.zh: 堅乃以高熲代昉為司馬；

translations.literal: Jian then replaced Fang with Gao Jiong as Chief Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian therefore replaced Fang with Gao Jiong as Chief Administrator;

sentences.zh: 不忍廢譯，陰敕官屬不得白事於譯。

translations.literal: unwilling to dismiss Yi outright, he secretly ordered the officials not to report business to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: unwilling to dismiss Yi outright, he secretly ordered the staff not to bring any business before Yi.

sentences.zh: 譯猶坐廳事，無所關預，惶懼頓首，求解職；

translations.literal: Yi still sat in the hall of business with nothing to decide; in fear and alarm he kowtowed and begged to be relieved of office;
translations.idiomatic: Yi still came and sat in the hall, but had nothing left to decide; terrified, he kowtowed and begged to be relieved of his post;

sentences.zh: 堅猶以恩禮慰勉之。

translations.literal: Jian still comforted and encouraged him with gracious treatment.
translations.idiomatic: yet Yang Jian still comforted him with words of favor and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 15癸酉，智武將軍魯廣達克周之郭默城。

translations.literal: 15. On guiyou, the Intelligent Martial General Lu Guangda captured Zhou's Guomo city.
translations.idiomatic: 15. On guiyou, Intelligent Martial General Lu Guangda of Chen captured Guomo, a Zhou stronghold.

sentences.zh: 丙子，淳於陵克祐州城。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Chunyu Ling captured Youzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Chunyu Ling took Youzhou city.

sentences.zh: 16周以漢王贊為太師，申公李穆為太傅，宋王實為大前疑，秦王贄為大右弼，燕公於寔為大左輔。

translations.literal: 16. Zhou appointed Prince of Han Zan as Grand Preceptor, Duke of Shen Li Mu as Grand Tutor, Prince of Song Shi as Grand Front Counselor, Prince of Qin Zhi as Grand Right Assistant, and Duke of Yan Yu Shi as Grand Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: 16. Northern Zhou made Prince of Han Zan Grand Preceptor, Duke of Shen Li Mu Grand Tutor, Prince of Song Shi Grand Front Counselor, Prince of Qin Zhi Grand Right Assistant, and Duke of Yan Yu Shi Grand Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 寔，仲文之父也。

translations.literal: Shi was Zhongwen's father.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shi was Yu Zhongwen's father.

sentences.zh: 17乙卯，周大赦。

translations.literal: 17. On yimao, Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: 17. On yimao, Northern Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 18周王誼帥四總管至鄖州，司馬消難擁其眾以魯山、甑山二鎮來降。

translations.literal: 18. Zhou Prince Yi led four governors to Yun prefecture. Sima Xiaonan brought his followers and surrendered with the two garrisons of Lushan and Zhenshan.
translations.idiomatic: 18. Northern Zhou's Prince Yi led four governors to Yun prefecture, where Sima Xiaonan came over with his followers, surrendering the garrisons at Lushan and Zhenshan.

sentences.zh: 初，消難遣上開府儀同大將軍段珣將兵圍順州，順州刺史周法尚不能拒，棄城走，消難虜其母弟而南。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiaonan had sent General of the Upper Gate with Equal Honor Duan Xun to lead troops and besiege Shun prefecture. Shun's governor Zhou Fashang could not hold out, abandoned the city and fled, and Xiaonan captured his mother and younger brother and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiaonan had sent General Duan Xun to besiege Shun prefecture. Governor Zhou Fashang could not hold the city, abandoned it and fled, and Xiaonan took his mother and younger brother captive before marching south.

sentences.zh: 樊毅救消難，不及。

translations.literal: Fan Yi went to rescue Xiaonan but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi marched to relieve Xiaonan but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 周亳州總管元景山擊之，毅掠居民而去。

translations.literal: Zhou's Bozhou governor Yuan Jingshan attacked him; Yi plundered the inhabitants and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jingshan, Zhou governor of Bozhou, struck at him; Fan Yi plundered the local people and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景山與南徐州刺史宇文弼追之，與毅戰於漳口。

translations.literal: Jingshan and Southern Xuzhou governor Yuwen Bi pursued him and fought Yi at Zhangkou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan and Yuwen Bi, governor of Southern Xuzhou, pursued him and fought Fan Yi at Zhangkou.

sentences.zh: 一日三戰三捷。

translations.literal: In one day they fought three battles and won three victories.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day they fought three engagements and won all three.

sentences.zh: 毅退保甑山鎮，城邑為消難所據者，景山皆復取之。

translations.literal: Yi fell back to hold Zhenshan garrison; every town and city that Xiaonan had occupied, Jingshan recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi fell back to Zhenshan garrison, and Jingshan recovered every town Xiaonan had held.

sentences.zh: 19鄖州巴蠻多叛，共推渠帥蘭雒州為主，以附消難。

translations.literal: 19. Many Ba tribesmen in Yun prefecture rebelled, jointly raising the chieftain Lan Luozhou as leader to join Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: 19. Many Ba tribes in Yun prefecture rose in rebellion, proclaiming the chieftain Lan Luozhou their leader and rallying to Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 王誼遣諸將分討之，旬月皆平。

translations.literal: Wang Yi sent generals to attack them separately; within a month all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi sent his generals against them in separate columns, and within a month all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳紀、蕭摩訶等攻廣陵，周吳州總管於顗擊破之。

translations.literal: Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, and others attacked Guangling; Zhou's Wuzhou governor Yu Yi defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, and others attacked Guangling, but Yu Yi, Zhou governor of Wuzhou, routed them.

sentences.zh: 沙州氐帥楊永安聚眾應王謙，大將軍樂寧公達奚儒討之。

translations.literal: Shazhou's Di chieftain Yang Yongan gathered a host in response to Wang Qian; Grand General Duke of Leping Da Xi Ru attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongan, Di chieftain of Shazhou, mustered followers in support of Wang Qian; Grand General Da Xi Ru, Duke of Leping, was sent against him.

sentences.zh: 楊素破宇文冑於石濟，斬之。

translations.literal: Yang Su defeated Yuwen Zhou at Shiji and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su defeated Yuwen Zhou at Shiji and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 20周以神武公竇毅為大司馬，齊公於智為大司空；

translations.literal: 20. Zhou appointed Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi as Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi Yu Zhi as Grand Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: 20. Northern Zhou appointed Dou Yi, Duke of Shenwu, Grand Marshal, and Yu Zhi, Duke of Qi, Grand Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 九月，以小宗伯竟陵公楊惠為大宗伯。

translations.literal: in the ninth month, Minor Minister of Rites Duke of Jingling Yang Hui was made Grand Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: and in the ninth month made Yang Hui, Duke of Jingling and former Minor Minister of Rites, Grand Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 21丁亥，周將王延貴帥眾援歷陽；

translations.literal: 21. On dinghai, Zhou general Wang Yangui led troops to relieve Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: 21. On dinghai, the Zhou general Wang Yangui led a force to relieve Liyang;

sentences.zh: 任忠擊破之，生擒延貴。

translations.literal: Ren Zhong defeated and broke them and captured Yangui alive.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong routed them and took Yangui alive.

sentences.zh: 22壬辰，周廢皇后司馬氏為庶人。

translations.literal: 22. On renchen, Zhou deposed Empress Sima and made her a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: 22. On renchen, Northern Zhou deposed Empress Sima and reduced her to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以隨世子勇為洛州總管、東京小塚宰，總統舊齊之地。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Sui heir Yong was made governor of Luozhou and Deputy Eastern Capital Chancellor, with overall charge of the old Qi territories.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Yang Yong, heir of the Duchy of Sui, was made governor of Luozhou and deputy chancellor of the Eastern Capital, with overall authority over the former Qi territories.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以左丞相堅為大丞相，罷左、右丞相之官。

translations.literal: On renzi, Left Chancellor Jian was made Grand Chancellor, and the offices of Left and Right Chancellor were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Left Chancellor Yang Jian was made Grand Chancellor, and the posts of left and right chancellor were abolished.

sentences.zh: 23冬，十月，甲寅，日有食之。

translations.literal: 23. In winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 23. In winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 24周丞相堅殺陳惑王純及其子。

translations.literal: 24. Zhou Chancellor Jian killed Prince of Chen Chun and his son.
translations.idiomatic: 24. Northern Zhou Chancellor Yang Jian executed Prince Chen Chun and his son.

sentences.zh: 25周梁睿將步騎二十萬討王謙，謙分命諸將據險拒守。

translations.literal: 25. Zhou's Liang Rui led two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Wang Qian. Qian dispatched his generals separately to hold strategic points and resist.
translations.idiomatic: 25. Liang Rui of Northern Zhou led two hundred thousand foot and horse against Wang Qian, who sent his generals to hold the defiles and resist.

sentences.zh: 睿奮擊，屢破之，蜀人大駭。

translations.literal: Rui fought fiercely and repeatedly defeated them; the people of Shu were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rui attacked with relentless force, breaking them again and again, and the people of Shu were terrified.

sentences.zh: 謙遣其將達奚惎、高阿那肱、乙弗虔等帥眾十萬攻利州，堰江水以灌之。

translations.literal: Qian sent his generals Da Xi Ji, Gao Anagun, Yifu Qian, and others to lead one hundred thousand men to attack Lizhou, damming the river waters to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent his generals Da Xi Ji, Gao Anagun, and Yifu Qian with one hundred thousand men against Lizhou, damming the river to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 城中戰士不過二千，總管昌黎豆盧勣，晝夜拒守，凡四旬，時出奇兵擊惎等，破之；

translations.literal: The fighting men in the city numbered no more than two thousand. Governor Dou Lu Ji of Changli defended day and night for forty days in all, and from time to time sent surprise forces to strike Ji and the others and defeat them;
translations.idiomatic: There were no more than two thousand defenders in the city. Governor Dou Lu Ji of Changli held out day and night for forty days, and more than once sent raiding parties against Ji and the others and drove them back;

sentences.zh: 會梁睿至，惎等遁去，睿自劍閣入，進逼成都。

translations.literal: When Liang Rui arrived, Ji and the others fled away. Rui entered through Jian'ge and advanced to press Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Rui arrived, Ji and his fellows withdrew; Rui came through Jian'ge and pressed on toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 謙令達奚惎、乙弗虔城守，親帥精兵五萬，背城結陳。

translations.literal: Qian ordered Da Xi Ji and Yifu Qian to hold the city while he personally led fifty thousand picked troops and formed battle lines with his back to the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qian left Da Xi Ji and Yifu Qian to defend the city while he personally led fifty thousand elite troops and drew up his battle line with the walls at his back.

sentences.zh: 睿擊之，謙戰敗，將入城，惎、虔以城降。

translations.literal: Rui attacked him. Qian was defeated in battle and was about to enter the city when Ji and Qian surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rui attacked and broke him. Qian was beaten and about to re-enter the city when Ji and Qian surrendered it.

sentences.zh: 謙將麾下三十騎走新都，新都令王寶執之。

translations.literal: Qian fled to Xindu with thirty horsemen from his personal following; Xindu's magistrate Wang Bao seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fled to Xindu with thirty horsemen from his personal guard; the magistrate of Xindu, Wang Bao, seized him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，睿斬謙及高阿那肱，劍南平。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Rui executed Qian and Gao Anagun, and Jiannan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Rui executed Qian and Gao Anagun, and the lands south of the passes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲辰，周達奚儒破楊永安，沙州平。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, Zhou's Da Xi Ru defeated Yang Yongan, and Shazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, Da Xi Ru of Northern Zhou defeated Yang Yongan and pacified Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，周鄖襄公韋孝寬卒。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Zhou's Duke of Yunxiang Wei Xiaokuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yunxiang, died.

sentences.zh: 孝寬久在邊境，屢抗強敵；

translations.literal: Xiaokuan had long been on the frontier and repeatedly resisted powerful enemies;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had spent years on the frontier, repeatedly facing down formidable foes;

sentences.zh: 所經略佈置，人初莫之解，見其成事，方乃驚服。

translations.literal: the measures he planned and deployed, at first no one understood them; only when they saw the results accomplished did they marvel and submit.
translations.idiomatic: his dispositions were often beyond understanding at first, and men admired them only after they saw how well they worked.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍中，篤意文史；

translations.literal: though he was in the army, he devoted himself earnestly to letters and learning;
translations.idiomatic: even in camp he devoted himself to letters and learning;

sentences.zh: 敦睦宗族，所得俸祿，不及私室。

translations.literal: he treated his clan with warmth and kindness, and the salary he received never reached his private household.
translations.idiomatic: he was generous to his clan, and none of his salary ever stayed in his own household.

sentences.zh: 人以此稱之。

translations.literal: People praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: People praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 26十二月，庚辰，河東康簡王叔獻卒。

translations.literal: 26. In the twelfth month, on gengchen, Prince Kangjian of Hedong, Chen Shuxian, died.
translations.idiomatic: 26. In the twelfth month, on gengchen, Prince Kangjian of Hedong, Chen Shuxian, died.

sentences.zh: 27癸亥，周詔諸改姓者，宜悉復舊。

translations.literal: 27. On guihai, Zhou issued an edict that all who had changed their surnames should fully restore their former names.
translations.idiomatic: 27. On guihai, Zhou ordered that everyone who had changed surnames under prior edicts should restore their original family names.

sentences.zh: 甲子，周以大丞相堅為相國，總百揆，去都督中外、大塚宰之號，進爵為王，以安陸等二十郡為隨國，贊拜不名，備九錫之禮；

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhou made the Grand Chancellor Jian Chancellor of State with overall charge of all affairs, removed the titles Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Within and Without and Grand Chamberlain, advanced his rank to prince, made Anlu and nineteen other commanderies the State of Sui, granted that he need not be addressed by name in memorials, and bestowed the full Nine Bestowals;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zhou made Grand Chancellor Yang Jian Chancellor of State with authority over all government, stripped him of the titles Commander-in-Chief of All Forces and Grand Chamberlain, raised him to prince, carved out the State of Sui from Anlu and nineteen other commanderies, granted him the privilege of being addressed without naming his name in memorials, and invested him with the full Nine Bestowals;

sentences.zh: 堅受王爵、十郡而已。

translations.literal: Jian accepted only the princely rank and ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian accepted only the princely title and ten commanderies, declining the rest.

sentences.zh: 辛未，殺代奰王達、滕聞王逌及其子。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Prince Daiyi of Dai, Da, and Prince Wen of Teng, You, were killed together with their sons.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Prince Daiyi of Dai, Da, and Prince Wen of Teng, You, were executed along with their sons.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以小塚宰元孝規為大司徒。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Junior Chamberlain Yuan Xiaogui was made Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Junior Chamberlain Yuan Xiaogui was appointed Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 28是歲，周境內有州二百一十一，郡五百八。

translations.literal: 28. That year, within Zhou's borders there were two hundred eleven provinces and five hundred eight commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: 28. That year, Zhou's territory comprised two hundred eleven provinces and five hundred eight commanderies.
